definition_zh: 不赞成；反对；不批准
definition_en: to think that something is wrong or unacceptable
core_image: 一只手在桌下轻轻摆了摆，示意别再往下说
scene: 他刚提到辞职，母亲就放下了手里的针线。 My father disapproves of late nights.
sceneCN: 这里 disapproves 指「不赞成」（第 1 个义项：认为不妥）；句意是我父亲不赞成熬夜。

derivatives.zh: 不赞成；反对
不以为然的
不以为然地
赞成；批准

senses.title: To judge an act as wrong
senses.definition: to think that a person's behaviour is not acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 认为某人的行为不可接受
senses.example: My father disapproves of late nights.
senses.exampleCN: 我父亲不赞成熬夜。
senses.why: The judgement comes first, and the sentence comes after.
senses.whyCN: 判断先到，话后到。

senses.title: To be against an idea
senses.definition: to think that a plan or idea should not go forward
senses.definitionCN: 认为某个计划或想法不该推进
senses.example: Most of the staff disapproved of the new rule.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数员工反对这条新规定。
senses.why: A plan is stopped in the mind before it is stopped in the office.
senses.whyCN: 计划先在脑子里被拦下，才在办公室里被拦下。

senses.title: To refuse official consent
senses.definition: to officially decide not to accept a request or a budget
senses.definitionCN: 正式决定不接受某项请求或预算
senses.example: The committee disapproved the new budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会没有批准新预算。
senses.why: The same judgement, once signed, closes a door.
senses.whyCN: 同一种判断，一签上字就关上了一扇门。

intro.en: Disapprove is dis- plus approve, whose Latin base approbare meant to test something as good.
intro.cn: disapprove 是 dis- 加 approve，其拉丁词基 approbare 指检验后认为好。

items.en: Probare meant to test, to prove or to judge.
items.cn: probare 指检验、证明或判断。

items.en: Approbare added ad- and meant to approve a thing.
items.cn: approbare 加上 ad-，表示认可某物。

items.en: Approve entered English with the sense of proving or commending.
items.cn: approve 进入英语时，指证明或称赞。

items.en: Disapprove reversed the judgement into a refusal.
items.cn: disapprove 把这份认可反转为否定。

items.en: The verb now covers private views and official decisions.
items.cn: 这个词既指私下看法，也指官方决定。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the approve stem, while the meaning group names other ways of saying no.
note.cn: 形近组共用 approve 这一段词干，近义组则列出其他说「不」的方式。

entries.definition: to think that something is good
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事好

entries.definition: a favourable judgement or consent
entries.definitionCN: 赞许的判断或同意

entries.definition: a judgement that something is wrong
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事不妥的判断

entries.definition: to say that one is against something
entries.definitionCN: 表示反对某事

entries.definition: to act against a plan or a person
entries.definitionCN: 采取行动反对某计划或某人

entries.definition: to regard something with clear disapproval
entries.definitionCN: 对某事明显不赞成

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a hand waved under a table to a stamp that is never given.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从桌下摆了一下的手，走到始终没有盖下的那枚章。

normal.en: Dis- plus approve: the approval is refused.
normal.cn: dis- 加 approve：认可被拒绝。

normal.en: A father disapproves with a look before a word.
normal.cn: 父亲往往先用眼神表示不赞成，然后才开口。

normal.en: Disapprove of a habit, and you judge the act, not the person.
normal.cn: 不赞成一种习惯，评的是行为，不是人。

normal.en: A committee can disapprove a budget with one vote.
normal.cn: 委员会一次投票就能不批准预算。

normal.en: The word leaves the thing standing, but withholds the yes.
normal.cn: 这个词让事情立着，却把那个「同意」扣下了。

abstract.en: Picture a hand waving low, out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在低处、在别人看不见的地方摆了摆。

abstract.en: Picture lips pressed while the eyes stay steady.
abstract.cn: 想象嘴唇抿紧，眼睛却一动不动。

abstract.en: Picture a form returned without a signature.
abstract.cn: 想象一份表格被退回，上面没有签名。

examples.en: My father disapproves of late nights.
examples.cn: 我父亲不赞成熬夜。

examples.en: The committee disapproved the new budget.
examples.cn: 委员会没有批准新预算。

examples.en: She disapproved of the way he spoke to the waiter.
examples.cn: 她不赞成他那样跟服务员说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disapprove 记成「的士不认」：司机不认这条路，摆手说不，就是不赞成。

root: 由否定前缀 dis- 加 approve 构成。approve 来自拉丁语 approbare（检验后认为好），词根 probare 意为检验、证明。加前缀后表示认为某事不妥，既可指私下的态度，也可指公开反对，甚至正式不予批准。

sensesIntro.en: From a private judgement of an act, to opposition to an idea, to an official no.
sensesIntro.cn: 从对行为的私下判断，到对想法的反对，再到官方的一声「不」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand waved low, telling someone to stop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在低处摆动，示意停下。

branches.en: The first sense is a judgement of behaviour.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是对行为的判断。

branches.en: The second sense is a stand against an idea.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是对某个想法的抵制。

branches.en: The third sense is the official refusal to consent.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是官方拒绝同意。

branches.en: A habit and a plan can both meet the same closed face.
branches.cn: 一种习惯和一个计划，可能撞上同一张合起来的脸。

branches.en: A spoken no becomes a formal no once it is recorded.
branches.cn: 说出的「不」一旦被记下，就成了正式的「不」。

intro.en: Disapprove belongs to the approve family, words about judging and consenting.
intro.cn: disapprove 属于 approve 一族，围绕评判与同意。

latinIntro.en: Latin probare, to test or prove, gives the prove in approve and disapprove.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 probare（检验、证明）给出 approve 与 disapprove 里的 prove。

items.example: They disapprove of the way the land is used.
items.exampleCN: 他们不赞成这块地的用法。
董事会批准了这个设计。

items.example: The plan is waiting for approval.

items.meaning: a judgement that something is wrong
items.example: His silence was a form of disapproval.
items.exampleCN: 他的沉默就是一种不赞成。

items.example: The teacher gave a disapproving look.
items.exampleCN: 老师投来不以为然的目光。

items.meaning: in a way that shows approval
items.example: He nodded approvingly at the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他赞许地对方案点了点头。

items.meaning: in a way that shows disapproval
items.example: She glanced disapprovingly at the mess.
items.exampleCN: 她不以为然地瞥了一眼那堆乱东西。

definition_zh: 漂流；漂移；趋势；要旨；堆积物；漂泊
definition_en: to be carried slowly by water or air, or a slow general movement or meaning
core_image: 一只空瓶随水流缓缓转向，没有人在掌舵
scene: 河面上起了风，一张纸片贴着水面慢慢滑向桥洞。 The empty boat began to drift toward the far bank.
sceneCN: 这里 drift 是「漂流」（第 1 个义项）；句意是那条空船开始向对岸漂去。

pos.zh: 动词：漂流；漂泊；逐渐变化
名词：漂流；趋势；要旨；堆积物

derivatives.zh: 由 drift 加 -er 构成，义为「漂泊不定的人」
由前缀 a-（处于……状态）加 drift 构成，义为「漂浮无依的」
由 drift 加 -ing 构成，义为「漂移的；漫无目的的」

senses.title: To be carried along by water or air
senses.definition: to move slowly on water or in the air without being controlled
senses.definitionCN: 在水面或空中缓慢移动，且不受控制
senses.example: The raft drifted out to sea during the night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里木筏漂到了海上。
senses.why: The word began as a noun for a driving force, then came to mean being driven along passively by water or wind.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「驱赶之力」，后来转指被水流或风被动地推着走，也就是漂流。

senses.title: To change or move gradually
senses.titleCN: 逐渐变化；不知不觉陷入
senses.definition: to move or change slowly, often without a clear plan
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢地移动或变化，往往没有明确计划
senses.example: The conversation drifted onto another subject.
senses.exampleCN: 谈话不知不觉转到了别的话题上。
senses.why: Speech that is not steered follows the current of thought the way a boat follows water, hence gradual unplanned change.
senses.whyCN: 没有被掌舵的谈话顺着思绪的水流走，正如船顺水而行，于是有了「不知不觉地变化」。

senses.title: A mass piled up by wind or water
senses.definition: a pile of snow, sand, or leaves heaped up by wind or water
senses.definitionCN: 被风或水堆起的一堆雪、沙或落叶
senses.example: A snow drift blocked the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 一堆积雪堵住了大门。
senses.why: Material carried by wind settles where the current slows, and the heap left behind takes the name of the drifting.
senses.whyCN: 被风带走的物质在气流变慢处落下，留下的一堆就沿用了「漂移」之名。

senses.title: The general meaning of what is said
senses.definition: the main point or general meaning of speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 言语或文字的主要意思与大致方向
senses.example: I did not catch the drift of his argument.
senses.exampleCN: 我没听懂他论证的大意。
senses.why: Meaning, like water, has a direction, so following the drift means following where the argument is heading.
senses.whyCN: 意义像水一样有方向，所以「顺着漂移」就是顺着论述要去的方向理解。

senses.title: A slow change in conditions or opinion
senses.definition: a gradual movement of prices, opinions, or events in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 价格、舆论或事件朝某一方向的缓慢移动
senses.example: There is a drift toward shorter working weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 现在存在一种朝更短工作周演变的趋势。
senses.why: Many small unforced movements add up to a direction, and that accumulated direction is also called a drift.
senses.whyCN: 许多微小的、非强制的移动累积成一个方向，这个累积出的方向也叫 drift。

intro.en: Drift comes from Old English drifan, to drive, and first named the act or force of driving.
intro.cn: drift 来自古英语 drifan（驱赶、推动），最初指「驱动」这一动作或力量。

items.en: A Germanic root meaning to drive lies behind the word; it is also the source of drive.
items.cn: 这个词背后有一个表示「驱赶」的日耳曼语词根，drive 也出自同一处。

items.en: Drifan meant to drive or force along, especially animals or ships.
items.cn: drifan 意为「驱赶、推动」，多用于牲畜或船只。

items.en: The noun drift named a driving force, then a slow course set by water or wind.
items.cn: 名词 drift 指驱动力，随后指由水流或风设定的缓慢路径。

items.en: The sense of a pile heaped by wind is recorded, and the meaning of general purport followed.
items.cn: 「被风堆起的一堆」这一义项有记录，随后又出现「大意、要旨」义。

items.en: The word extended to gradual social and economic trends and to aimless wandering.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到社会与经济的渐变趋势，以及漫无目的的漂泊。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the driving root; the near-meaning group separates floating from wandering.
note.cn: 形近组共享「驱动」词根；近义组把「漂浮」与「漫游」分开。

entries.definition: To operate a vehicle or to force something forward.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「驾驶；驱动」，与 drift 同源。

entries.definition: A person who moves from place to place without a fixed home.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「漂泊者」，由 drift 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Floating without control or without a fixed course.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「漂流无依的」，由 a- 加 drift 构成。

entries.definition: To rest on water without sinking, without implying movement.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「漂浮」，只讲不沉，不含移动。

entries.definition: To walk around without a clear direction, usually on land.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「漫游」，多指陆地行走。

entries.definition: A general direction in which something is developing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「趋势」，与 drift 的第五个义项接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow one driving root into water, speech, snow and social change.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着同一个「驱动」词根，走进水、言语、积雪与社会变化。

normal.en: Drift and drive are cousins: one pushes, the other is pushed along.
normal.cn: drift 与 drive 是表亲：一个在推，一个被推着走。

normal.en: A boat with no one at the wheel can only drift.
normal.cn: 没人掌舵的船只能漂流。

normal.en: Speech that loses its steering drifts onto other topics.
normal.cn: 失去操控的谈话就会漂到别的话题上。

normal.en: Snow carried by wind is left as a drift at the gate.
normal.cn: 被风带走的雪会在大门处堆成一堆。

normal.en: Catch the drift means follow where the meaning is flowing.
normal.cn: catch the drift 就是顺着意义流动的方向听懂大意。

abstract.en: Picture an empty bottle turning slowly in a current.
abstract.cn: 想象一只空瓶在水流里缓缓转向。

abstract.en: Picture snow piling against a wall in a long wedge.
abstract.cn: 想象雪在墙边堆成一条长长的楔形。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation sliding off its first topic.
abstract.cn: 想象一场谈话从最初的话题上滑开。

examples.en: The balloon drifted east with the morning wind.
examples.cn: 气球随晨风向东飘去。

examples.en: He drifted off before the film had ended.
examples.cn: 电影还没放完他就睡着了。

examples.en: The drift of her letter was that she needed more time.
examples.cn: 她那封信的大意是她需要更多时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「追风」——被风追着走、自己在动却没有方向，就是 drift 的「漂流、渐趋」。

root: 来自古英语 drifan（驱赶、推动），属日耳曼语词族，与 drive 同源。本义为「驱动」，后转为「被水流或风推着走」，再引申为「堆积物」「大意」「逐渐变化的趋势」与「漂泊」。

sensesIntro.en: One image of being pushed without steering covers water, speech, snow heaps, and slow social change.
sensesIntro.cn: 「被推着走却无人掌舵」这一个画面，覆盖水上漂流、谈话转向、积雪成堆与缓慢的社会变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty bottle turning slowly in a current.
core.cn: 核心意象：空瓶在水流里缓缓转向。

branches.en: WATER AND AIR: the physical sense is passive movement on a current.
branches.cn: 水与风线：物理义是在水流中被动移动，即第一个义项。

branches.en: CHANGE: unsteered movement becomes gradual drift in talk and in society.
branches.cn: 变化线：无人操控的移动变成谈话与社会的渐变，即第二、五个义项。

branches.en: THE HEAP: what a current drops stays as a drift.
branches.cn: 堆积线：水流或风放下的东西留成一堆，即第三个义项。

branches.en: MEANING: following the drift is following where the sense flows.
branches.cn: 意义线：顺着漂移走，就是顺着意义流动的方向，即第四个义项。

branches.en: Water and words share a current, which is why both can be drifted along.
branches.cn: 水与言语共享一股「流」，所以两者都能被顺着带走。

intro.en: Drift is a Germanic root word that accepts English endings and a small prefix.
intro.cn: drift 是日耳曼语根词，可接英语词尾与一个小前缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in drift itself; the noun ending -er and the prefix a- are English.
latinIntro.cn: drift 本身没有拉丁成分；名词词尾 -er 与前缀 a- 都是英语的。

items.example: The verb is the source of both drive and drift.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时是 drive 与 drift 的来源。

derivatives.zh: 由 drift 加 -er 构成，义为「漂泊者」
由 a- 加 drift 构成，义为「漂流无依的」

definition_zh: 不确定的；无把握的；无法确定的；无常的；犹豫的
definition_en: not sure or not known, and therefore liable to change
core_image: 雾里的一条岔路，看不清哪一条通向哪里
scene: 出发前夜，一家人围着地图讨论路线，天气预报却每小时都在改。 The date of the wedding is still uncertain.
sceneCN: 这里 uncertain 是「不确定的、未定的」（第 1 个义项：不能确定是否或何时）；句意为婚礼的日期还没定下来。雾中岔路看不清，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：不确定的；无把握的
形容词：变化无常的；靠不住的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ty 构成名词，义为「不确定性；疑虑」
形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不肯定地；迟疑地」
去掉否定前缀的原词，义为「确定的」

senses.title: Not known for sure
senses.definition: not established as a fact, and so open to doubt
senses.definitionCN: 尚未确定成为事实，因此存疑
senses.example: The cause of the fire is still uncertain.
senses.exampleCN: 起火原因仍未确定。
senses.why: Certain comes from Latin certus, settled, so uncertain is what has not been settled.
senses.whyCN: certain 源自拉丁语 certus（已定的），uncertain 就是「尚未被定下来的」。

senses.title: Not confident in one’s own mind
senses.definition: feeling doubt about one’s knowledge or judgement
senses.definitionCN: 对自己的知识或判断感到怀疑
senses.example: I am uncertain about the wording of the rule.
senses.exampleCN: 我对这条规则的确切措辞没有把握。
senses.why: When the fact is not settled, the mind that holds it also cannot settle.
senses.whyCN: 事实没有落定，心里装着它的人也落定不了。

senses.title: Likely to change and unreliable
senses.definition: unsteady, and likely to shift without warning
senses.definitionCN: 不稳定，随时可能无预警地改变
senses.example: This region has uncertain rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区的降雨很不稳定。
senses.why: Details that are not fixed produce conditions that cannot be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 没有定下来的细节，造出不能信赖的状况。

senses.title: Hesitant in movement or manner
senses.definition: moving or speaking in a way that shows doubt
senses.definitionCN: 动作或说话显出犹疑
senses.example: He took an uncertain step toward the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他迟疑地朝门口迈了一步。
senses.why: The body copies the mind: a doubtful thought produces a hesitant step.
senses.whyCN: 身体会照着心走：犹豫的念头生犹疑的脚步。

senses.title: Not definitely good or bad
senses.definition: of an outcome, still open to either result
senses.definitionCN: 就结果而言，两种可能都还在
senses.example: The election result remains uncertain.
senses.exampleCN: 选举结果仍未可知。
senses.why: An open path with fog on it has not yet shown which way it leads.
senses.whyCN: 一条起雾的岔路，还没显出它通向哪边。

intro.en: The word is an English negative built on a Latin adjective of settled fact.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语否定形式，建在一个表示「已定事实」的拉丁形容词上。

items.en: Certus means sure, settled, or decided, from cernere, to sift and decide.
items.cn: certus 意为确定的、已定的，源自 cernere（筛选、判定）。

items.en: Old French certain carries the adjective into English with the sense of assured.
items.cn: 古法语 certain 把这个形容词带入英语，意为「保证的」。

items.en: English uses certain for what is firmly known, especially in the phrase for certain.
items.cn: 英语用 certain 指确实知道的事，尤见于 for certain 一语。

items.en: Un- is added to form the negative from the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十四世纪起加 un- 构成否定。

items.en: The idiom in no uncertain terms keeps the negated form for emphasis.
items.cn: 习语 in no uncertain terms 用否定形式来加强语气。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the cert- family, and the near-meaning group gathers words of doubt.
note.cn: 形近组展示 cert- 词族，近义组汇集表示怀疑的词。

entries.definition: without doubt
entries.definitionCN: 肯定地；当然

entries.definition: the state of being sure
entries.definitionCN: 确信；必然

entries.definition: to state officially that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 证明；发证

entries.definition: unlikely or full of doubt
entries.definitionCN: 可疑的；拿不准的

entries.definition: not confident about something
entries.definitionCN: 没有把握的

entries.definition: not clear in detail
entries.definitionCN: 含糊的

entries.definition: sure and settled
entries.definitionCN: 确定的

normalIntro.en: Certus in Latin means sifted and settled, and the prefix simply takes that away.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语 certus 意为筛过、定下，前缀只是把它拿走。

normal.en: Certus comes from cernere, to sift, so an uncertain fact has not been sifted out yet.
normal.cn: certus 源自 cernere（筛拣），uncertain 的事实还没被筛清。

normal.en: Certainty and uncertainty are the two nouns, one settled and one not.
normal.cn: certainty 与 uncertainty 是两枚名词，一个已定，一个未定。

normal.en: In no uncertain terms is the fixed idiom meaning very clearly.
normal.cn: in no uncertain terms 是固定习语，意为非常明确地。

normal.en: Uncertainty is uncountable in general use but takes -ies for particular doubts.
normal.cn: uncertainty 泛指时不可数，说具体的疑虑时可用复数 uncertainties。

normal.en: Uncertain usually leads to about, as in uncertain about the details.
normal.cn: uncertain 常跟 about 搭配，如 uncertain about the details。

abstract.en: Stand where one road splits in fog and both branches fade.
abstract.cn: 站在雾里岔路口，两条岔路都渐渐淡掉。

abstract.en: Hold a coin before it lands, both sides still possible.
abstract.cn: 捏着一枚将落未落的硬币，两面都还成立。

abstract.en: Feel your own foot lift with no certainty where it will fall.
abstract.cn: 感觉自己的脚抬起来，却不知会落在哪里。

examples.en: Her tone was polite but uncertain.
examples.cn: 她的语气客气却没有把握。

examples.en: It is uncertain whether the match will be played tomorrow.
examples.cn: 明天是否比赛还不确定。

examples.en: He left in no uncertain terms that he disagreed.
examples.cn: 他非常明确地表示自己不同意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安色疼」——心上不踏实，像针扎一样隐隐作疼。

root: un-（否定前缀）+ certain（拉丁语 certus「确定的」，源自 cernere「筛拣、判定」）；同族有 certainty、certainly、certify

sensesIntro.en: Each sense is a piece of fog: an unknown fact, a doubtful mind, unsteady conditions, hesitant movement, an open result.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都是一片雾：未知的事实、没底的心里、不稳的条件、迟疑的动作、未定的结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forked road disappearing into fog.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条岔路消失在雾里。

branches.en: The fact branch: what is not known and what has not been decided.
branches.cn: 事实分支：不知道的与未决定的。

branches.en: The mind branch: confidence that has not formed.
branches.cn: 心理分支：尚未形成的把握。

branches.en: The condition branch: weather and figures that shift.
branches.cn: 状况分支：会变动的天气与数字。

branches.en: The manner branch: a step or a voice full of doubt.
branches.cn: 方式分支：充满疑虑的脚步或嗓音。

branches.en: The plain sense used about dates and causes.
branches.cn: 谈论日期与原因时最常用的义项。

intro.en: A negation prefix over a Latin word meaning sifted and settled.
intro.cn: 否定前缀盖在「筛过、定下」的拉丁词上。

latinIntro.en: The cern- root also yields discern, decide, and discriminate.
latinIntro.cn: cern- 词根还生出 discern、decide、discriminate。

items.exampleCN: cernere 支撑着 decide 与 discern。

items.example: Certain keeps the Latin ending in English dress.
items.exampleCN: certain 以英语外衣保留拉丁语词尾。

definition_zh: 值得做的；值得花时间的；值得花力气的；有价值的
definition_en: worth the time, effort or money spent on it
core_image: 一趟跋涉之后站在山顶，疲劳还在，心里却说不虚此行
scene: 花了三年改稿，书终于出版，作者说这三年没白费。 It is worthwhile checking the figures before you send the report.
sceneCN: 这里 worthwhile 是「值得做的」（第 1 个义项：花的时间与力气有回报）；句意为发报告前把数据核一遍是值得的。爬到山顶说不虚此行的感觉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：值得做的、值得花时间的、值得花力气的

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「价值」，是合成词的前半部分
名词，义为「一段时间」，是合成词的后半部分
副词，义为「无价值地」，属反面一支
形容词，义为「值得的、可敬的」，同族
介词，义为「值、值得」，常与 doing 连用

senses.title: Worth the time given
senses.titleCN: 值得做：花掉的时间有回报
senses.definition: worth the time spent on it
senses.definitionCN: 花在上面的时间有回报
senses.example: It is worthwhile checking the figures before you send the report.
senses.exampleCN: 发报告前把数据核一遍是值得的。
senses.why: The word joins worth, value, to while, a stretch of time: the value must cover the time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 worth「价值」与 while「一段时间」拼在一起：价值必须抵得过时间。

senses.title: Worth the effort
senses.titleCN: 值得费力：辛苦没有白费
senses.definition: worth the effort and difficulty involved
senses.definitionCN: 付出的力气与困难有回报
senses.example: The climb was hard, but the view made it worthwhile.
senses.exampleCN: 爬山很辛苦，但风景让这趟很值。
senses.why: Effort is a cost like money, and the word can be paid in it too.
senses.whyCN: 力气是和金钱一样的成本，这个词也接受用力气付款。

senses.title: Worth the money
senses.titleCN: 值得花钱：投入能收回来
senses.definition: worth the money paid for it
senses.definitionCN: 付出的钱能收回来
senses.example: The repairs were expensive but worthwhile in the long run.
senses.exampleCN: 修理费很贵，但长远看是值得的。
senses.why: Cost and benefit sit in the same sentence, and the word decides for the benefit.
senses.whyCN: 成本与收益被放进同一个句子，而这个词判给了收益。

senses.title: Worth doing at all
senses.titleCN: 有价值的：事情本身有意义
senses.definition: having real value or importance, said of causes and work
senses.definitionCN: 本身具有真实价值，用于事业与工作
senses.example: She found the work worthwhile even though the pay was low.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得这份工作很有意义，尽管报酬很低。
senses.why: Here the return is not money but meaning, the widest kind of while that worth can cover.
senses.whyCN: 这里的回报不是钱而是意义，这是 worth 能抵付的最宽的一种时间。

intro.en: Worthwhile is a late English compound: worth, value, plus while, a period of time, meaning worth the time.
intro.cn: worthwhile 是较晚出现的英语合成词：worth「价值」加 while「一段时间」，即「值这段时间」。

items.en: The noun weorth meant value or price, and the preposition use came later.
items.cn: 名词 weorth 意为价值或价钱，介词用法出现较晚。

items.en: The noun hwil meant a period of time, source of modern while.
items.cn: 名词 hwil 意为一段时间，是现代 while 的来源。

items.en: Worthwhile appeared as a compound in the nineteenth century, first in American writing.
items.cn: worthwhile 作为合成词在十九世纪出现，最早见于美国文字。

items.en: Modern usage often follows worth one’s while and it is worthwhile doing.
items.cn: 现代用法常见 worth one’s while 与 it is worthwhile doing 两种句式。

items.en: The word spread from business and education into general judgements of effort.
items.cn: 这个词从商业与教育扩展到对一切付出的总体评价。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the worth- family and the while compound; the near-meaning group holds words for being worth something.
note.cn: 形近组沿 worth- 家族与 while 合成词；近义组收表示值得的词。

entries.definition: Value, or the preposition meaning deserving of.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或介词，义为「价值、值得」，本词前半部。

entries.definition: A period of time; the second half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一段时间」，本词后半部。

entries.definition: Deserving of respect or effort, used of people and causes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「值得的、可敬的」，用于人与事业。

entries.definition: Having no value, the negative cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无价值的」，反面的近亲。

entries.definition: Worth a lot, often in money or usefulness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有价值的」，多指金钱或效用。

entries.definition: Giving satisfaction for the effort made.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有回报的」，强调满足感。

entries.definition: Helpful for a purpose, without the cost comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有用的」，不含成本比较。

entries.definition: Not worth doing at all, the opposite judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「毫无意义的」，相反的判断。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal sum inside the compound: value versus time spent.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用合成词里那笔字面账：价值对花掉的时间。

normal.en: Worthwhile is worth plus while: the value must cover the time.
normal.cn: worthwhile 是 worth 加 while：价值要抵得住时间。

normal.en: It is worthwhile doing is the standard pattern before a gerund.
normal.cn: worthwhile 后接动名词时常用 it is worthwhile doing 的句式。

normal.en: Well worthwhile adds emphasis but changes nothing else.
normal.cn: well worthwhile 只是加强语气，其余不变。

normal.en: Worthy describes people and causes, worthwhile describes time and effort.
normal.cn: worthy 说人与事业，worthwhile 说时间与力气。

normal.en: Make it worthwhile means add something so the effort pays.
normal.cn: make it worthwhile 指加点东西让这份辛苦有回报。

abstract.en: The compound hides an economics of life: every yes to one thing is a no to the hours it takes.
abstract.cn: 这个合成词藏着一门生活经济学：对一件事说「好」，就是对它占用的钟点说「不」。

abstract.en: Value here is judged afterwards as well as before; that is why we say it proved worthwhile.
abstract.cn: 这里的价值既在事前判断也在事后判断，所以说 it proved worthwhile。

abstract.en: Anything worth the while is worth it to someone, which is why the word never settles a question by itself.
abstract.cn: 值不值总是对某个人而言，所以这个词从不能独自断案。

examples.en: It is worthwhile keeping a copy of every letter.
examples.cn: 每封信都留个副本是值得的。

examples.en: The extra training proved worthwhile in the end.
examples.cn: 额外的培训最终证明是值得的。

examples.en: They made the trip worthwhile by staying an extra week.
examples.cn: 他们多待了一周，让这趟行程更值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃思外偶」——沃思（我思）外偶（外哦），外面走走也值得：值得做的

root: 由 worth「价值」与 while「一段时间」在十九世纪合成，意为「值得花这段时间的」；同族词有 worth、worthy、worthless。

sensesIntro.en: Worthwhile measures the return on time, effort, money, or the plain value of the work itself.
sensesIntro.cn: worthwhile 衡量的是对时间、力气、金钱的回报，或工作本身的价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing on a summit, tired but certain the climb was not wasted.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在山顶，累却确定这趟没白爬。

branches.en: TIME LINE: hours spent and repaid.
branches.cn: 时间线：花掉的钟点被偿还。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the effort paid off.
branches.cn: 身体线：力气有了回报。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: the cost comes back.
branches.cn: 金钱线：成本收得回来。

branches.en: MEANING LINE: the work matters in itself.
branches.cn: 意义线：工作本身就有价值。

branches.en: CONTRAST: worthwhile is about return, worthy is about merit.
branches.cn: 对照线：worthwhile 讲回报，worthy 讲品格。

intro.en: Worthwhile is a compound of two whole English words; nothing is glued on with an affix.
intro.cn: worthwhile 是两个完整英语词的合成，没有使用词缀粘接。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin here; both halves are Old English nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分，前后两半都是古英语名词。

items.example: It forms worthwhileness in rare use.
It appears in older forms of the compound.
It is the full phrase behind it.
items.exampleCN: 它是本词背后的完整说法。

definition_zh: 忽视；疏忽；漏做；疏于照料
definition_en: to fail to give proper care or attention to a person or thing; to leave a duty undone; and the state of being left without care
core_image: 一盆没人浇水的花，土面干裂，叶子垂到桌沿
scene: 窗台上的花盆积了灰，土面裂开细缝，枝叶一路垂到桌沿。 Nobody had watered the plants in weeks, and the whole corner looked neglected.
sceneCN: 这里 neglect 是「疏于照料」（第 1 个义项：该照顾却没有照顾）；句意为几个星期没人浇水，角落里的植物一副被冷落的样子。图中可辨识物件：花盆、干裂的土、垂下的叶子。

pos.zh: 疏忽；失职；被冷落的状态

derivatives.zh: 由 neglect 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「疏忽的；不留心的」
与 neglect 同出拉丁语 neglegere，经法语进入英语，义为「疏忽；过失」
同出拉丁语 neglegere，由拉丁语 neglegentia 而来，义为「疏忽的；失职的」
同出拉丁语 neglegere（不去拾取），义为「微不足道的；可忽略的」

senses.title: To fail to care for someone or something
senses.definition: to fail to give the care and attention that a person, an animal or a thing needs
senses.definitionCN: 没有给予人、动物或事物所需的照料与关注
senses.example: The owner neglected the dog for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 主人几个星期都没好好照顾那只狗。
senses.why: The Latin verb neglegere is neg- plus legere, literally not to pick up, so the sense begins as care that is left lying on the ground instead of being taken up.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 neglegere 由否定成分 neg- 与 legere（拾取）组成，字面是「不去拾取」，所以这个义项的起点是：本该被照看的东西被撂在地上，没人伸手。

senses.title: To pay no attention to advice or warning
senses.definition: to give no attention to advice, a rule, a warning or a risk that should be taken seriously
senses.definitionCN: 对本该认真对待的建议、规定、警告或风险不予理会
senses.example: The company neglected the safety rules for years.
senses.exampleCN: 多年来公司一直无视安全规定。
senses.why: If the basic gesture is not reaching down for something, then a warning lying in plain sight can also go unpicked, since the information is there but nobody bothers to take it.
senses.whyCN: 如果基本动作是不肯伸手去拿，那么明摆着的警告同样会没人去拿：信息就在眼前，只是无人愿意伸手。

senses.title: To leave a task or duty undone
senses.definition: to fail to do something that one is responsible for doing, especially through carelessness
senses.definitionCN: 因粗心等原因没有完成自己应做的事
senses.example: He neglected to lock the door before leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 他走之前忘了锁门。
senses.why: The same picture explains the infinitive pattern: a duty is something placed in front of you, and this word means walking past it without picking it up.
senses.whyCN: 同一个画面也解释了后面接不定式的句式：责任像放在眼前的东西，这个词表示走过去却没有把它拿起来。

senses.title: The state of being left without care
senses.definition: the condition of having been left without proper care, or the failure to provide that care
senses.definitionCN: 被撇下、无人照管的状态，或没有尽到照管责任的行为
senses.example: The old theatre slowly fell into neglect.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老剧院慢慢荒废了。
senses.why: Turning the verb into an uncountable noun freezes the act of not picking something up into a lasting condition, so a building can remain inside that condition for years.
senses.whyCN: 把动词变成不可数名词之后，「不去拾取」这个动作凝成一种持续的状态，于是一栋建筑可以在这种状态里一放多年。

intro.en: Neglect goes back to a Latin verb that literally means not to pick something up, and the picture of a thing left lying explains most of its senses.
intro.cn: neglect 上溯到一个字面意为「不去拾取」的拉丁动词，东西被撂下不管的画面能解释它的大部分义项。

items.en: Legere meant to pick up, to gather or to choose, and it stands behind many words about reading and selecting.
items.cn: legere 意为拾取、收集或挑选，是许多与阅读、选择有关的词的源头。

items.en: The verb neglegere joined neg-, not, with legere, so it meant not to pick up, and from that, to disregard.
items.cn: 动词 neglegere 把否定成分 neg- 与 legere 结合，意为「不去拾取」，由此引申为「不理会」。

items.en: Its past participle neglectus meant unheeded or slighted, and this form accounts for the ct in the English spelling.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 neglectus 意为「被忽略的、被轻视的」，英语拼写里的 ct 就来自这个形式。

items.en: The word reached English through French forms of the same verb, and Middle English used it for leaving a duty or a person untended.
items.cn: 这个词经同一动词的法语形式进入英语，中古英语用它表示搁下职责或不去照管某人。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb and adds an uncountable noun for the resulting state, which is how a building comes to fall into neglect.
items.cn: 现代英语保留动词，又添一个不可数名词表示由此产生的状态，建筑 fall into neglect 的说法就是这样来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same Latin stem of not picking up; the near-meaning group gathers words for paying no attention.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「不去拾取」拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示不加理会的词。

entries.definition: Failing to take the care that a job or duty requires.
entries.definitionCN: 未尽应有照管的；失职的。

entries.definition: The failure to take reasonable care, especially when it causes harm.
entries.definitionCN: 未采取合理注意而导致损害的过失；疏忽。

entries.definition: So small or slight that it can safely be ignored.
entries.definitionCN: 小到可以放心忽略的；微不足道的。

entries.definition: To pay no attention to someone or something, often on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 故意不理会某人或某物。

entries.definition: To treat something as not worth attention or respect.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事视为不值得注意或尊重。

entries.definition: To fail to notice something, usually without intending to.
entries.definitionCN: 没注意到某事，通常并非故意。

normalIntro.en: The word lives on the Latin image of not picking something up, and its family spreads that image across care, duty and reading.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词活在「不去拾取」的拉丁画面上，它的同族词把这一画面铺到照料、职责和阅读上。

normal.en: Legere means to pick up, so neglegere is the gesture of leaving something exactly where it lies.
normal.cn: legere 意为拾取，neglegere 就是把手收回来、让东西留在原地。

normal.en: Negligence is the noun of the same stem, and in law it names a failure of care rather than a deliberate act.
normal.cn: negligence 是同一词干的名词，在法律里它指照管上的缺失，而不是故意行为。

normal.en: Negligible keeps the idea of not worth picking up, so it describes something too small to matter.
normal.cn: negligible 保留「不值得拾取」的意思，所以形容小到不值得计较的东西。

normal.en: The pattern with an infinitive takes a duty as its object, while the pattern with a noun takes a person or a thing.
normal.cn: 接不定式的句式把职责作宾语，接名词的句式则把人或物作宾语。

normal.en: Benign neglect is a fixed phrase for harm that comes from being left alone rather than from any action.
normal.cn: benign neglect 是固定说法，指因放着不管而非因动手造成的伤害。

abstract.en: A word that began as a hand refusing to reach down still carries the quiet violence of leaving something to spoil.
abstract.cn: 一个从「手不肯伸下去」开始的词，仍带着把东西放着坏掉的隐秘暴力。

abstract.en: Neglect is usually a sin of omission, which is why it leaves no scene to point at, only a gap.
abstract.cn: neglect 通常是一种不作为的过失，所以它没有场面可指，只留下一片空白。

abstract.en: The same stem gave English both reading and neglect: what is never picked up can never be read.
abstract.cn: 同一词干给了英语「阅读」与「疏忽」两族词：没被拾起的东西自然没法读。

examples.en: The garden had been neglected for years before the new owner took it over.
examples.cn: 新主人接手之前，这座花园已经多年无人打理。

examples.en: The report says the company neglected basic safety checks.
examples.cn: 报告称公司忽视了基本的安全检查。

examples.en: She neglected to tell us that the meeting had moved.
examples.cn: 她忘了告诉我们会议改了地点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「懒得理」——看见了却懒得理会，东西就被撂下；记住 neglect 是忽视、疏于照料。

root: 拉丁语 legere（拾取、挑选）加否定成分 neg- 构成 neglegere（不去拾取），过去分词 neglectus；经法语进入英语，动词与名词同形。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is care that is never taken up; from it come the ignoring of warnings, the forgetting of duties and the lasting state of being left untended.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「该被拾起的照料始终没人伸手」；由此分出对警告的无视、对职责的漏做，以及长期无人照管的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pot of cracked dry soil on a sill, with leaves hanging over the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗台上一盆干裂的土，叶子垂到桌沿。

branches.en: a dog waiting by an empty bowl all afternoon
branches.cn: 一只狗在空碗边等了整个下午

branches.en: a house with shutters closed for many seasons
branches.cn: 好几个季节都关着窗板的房子

branches.en: a warning sign half hidden behind tall grass
branches.cn: 被高草遮住一半的警示牌

branches.en: an unlocked door left swinging in the wind
branches.cn: 没锁的门被风吹得来回晃

definition_zh: 惊叫；大声说；呼喊
definition_en: to cry out suddenly because of strong feeling
core_image: 拆开礼物时脱口而出的惊呼
scene: 看到礼物时，她惊讶地叫了出来。 When she saw the gift, she exclaimed in surprise.
sceneCN: 这里 exclaim 是「惊叫」（第 1 个义项：因强烈情绪突然喊出）；句意：看到礼物时，她惊讶地叫了出来。

senses.title: A sudden cry
senses.definition: to cry out suddenly from surprise or shock
senses.definitionCN: 因惊讶或震惊突然喊出
senses.example: She exclaimed when she opened the box.
senses.exampleCN: 她打开盒子时惊叫了一声。
senses.why: Strong feeling jumps out before thought.
senses.whyCN: 强烈情绪先于思考冲了出来。

senses.title: A loud protest
senses.definition: to say something loudly with strong feeling, often disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 带着强烈情绪大声说出，常表示反对
senses.example: He exclaimed that the plan was unfair.
senses.exampleCN: 他大声说这个计划不公平。
senses.why: Anger also pushes words into the open.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒同样把话语推到明处。

intro.en: Exclaim comes from Latin exclamare, to call out.
intro.cn: exclaim 源自拉丁语 exclamare，意为喊出。

items.en: Clamare means to shout.
items.cn: clamare 意为喊叫。

items.en: Exclamare joins ex-, out, with clamare, to shout.
items.cn: exclamare 由 ex-（出）与 clamare（喊）组成。

items.en: French exclamer keeps the sudden cry.
items.cn: 法语 exclamer 保留突然呼喊之意。

items.en: English exclaim marks surprise or protest.
items.cn: 英语 exclaim 表示惊讶或抗议。

items.en: Exclamation marks appear in writing.
items.cn: 感叹号出现在书面语中。

note.en: Exclaim is sudden and emotional; say is neutral.
note.cn: exclaim 突然而带情绪，say 是中性的。

entries.definition: a sudden cry or a mark of it

entries.definition: to shout suddenly

entries.definitionCN: 脱口而出

normalIntro.en: To exclaim is to let a feeling speak.
normalIntro.cn: exclaim 就是让情绪直接说话。

normal.en: Exclaim in surprise means cry out suddenly.
normal.cn: exclaim in surprise 意为突然惊叫。

normal.en: Exclaim at means react loudly to something.
normal.cn: exclaim at 意为对某物大声反应。

normal.en: Exclaim with delight means cheer.

normal.en: Exclaim loudly means raise your voice.

abstract.en: Imagine words jumping out before thought.

abstract.en: Think of a loud voice cutting through a room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个响亮的声音穿过房间。

examples.en: She exclaimed at the size of the fish.
examples.cn: 她惊叹这条鱼真大。

examples.en: He exclaimed that he had won.
examples.cn: 他大声宣布自己赢了。

examples.en: The crowd exclaimed in delight.
examples.cn: 人群高兴地欢呼起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ claim（喊）」——把话喊出来，就是惊叫。

root: 拉丁语 exclamare（喊出）＝ ex-（出）＋ clamare（喊）→ exclaim，核心义「情绪驱使下突然喊出」。

sensesIntro.en: Exclaim means to cry out suddenly in surprise or to say something loudly in protest.
sensesIntro.cn: exclaim 意为因惊讶突然喊出，或带情绪大声抗议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words jumping out before thought.
core.cn: 核心意象：话语先于思考蹦出。

branches.en: Surprise makes the words jump out.
branches.cn: 惊讶让话语冲出。

branches.en: Protest sends the voice upward.

branches.en: Joy and anger both push words outward.
