definition_zh: 誓言；承诺；抵押物；发誓；抵押
definition_en: a serious promise, or something handed over as security for a debt, and the act of promising or depositing it
core_image: 举起的右手和一张写好的承诺书，说出口就要兑现
scene: 毕业典礼上，全体新生举起右手，跟着领誓人一句一句念出承诺。 Each new member had to pledge loyalty to the group in front of everyone.
sceneCN: 这里用的是动词「郑重许诺」（第 3 个义项：发誓、保证）；句意为每位新成员都得当众承诺忠于这个团体。画面里有举起的右手、台下的同伴和安静下来的会场。

collocations.zh: 发誓献身于；保证致力于

derivatives.zh: 由 pledge 加表示承受方的后缀 -ee 构成，法律上指「接受质押的人」
由 pledge 加表示行为方的后缀 -or 构成，法律上指「出质人；抵押人」
由否定前缀 un- 加 pledge 的过去分词构成，义为「未作承诺的；未抵押的」

senses.title: A solemn promise
senses.definition: a serious promise that you will do something, especially one made in public
senses.definitionCN: 郑重许下、通常当众作出的承诺
senses.example: The government broke its pledge to protect the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 政府违背了保护这片森林的承诺。
senses.why: The word first named a thing handed over as a guarantee; a spoken promise borrowed that image because a word can also be held against you.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指交出去的担保物；口头承诺借用同一意象，因为一句话同样可以日后被人拿来对着你算账。

senses.title: Something given as security
senses.definition: an object or sum left with someone as security until a debt is paid or a duty is met
senses.definitionCN: 为担保债务或义务而交给对方保管的物件或款项
senses.example: He left his watch as a pledge for the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他把手表留下作为这笔借款的抵押。
senses.why: In medieval law a pledge was the item physically held, so the object and the promise shared one name from the start.
senses.whyCN: 在中世纪的法律里，pledge 就是被实际扣在手里的那件东西，所以「物」与「诺」从一开始就共用一个名字。

senses.title: To promise solemnly
senses.definition: to promise seriously and publicly that you will do something or stay loyal
senses.definitionCN: 郑重而公开地保证要做某事或保持忠诚
senses.example: The company pledged to cut its emissions by half.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司承诺把排放量削减一半。
senses.why: The verb grew out of the noun: to pledge is to hand over your word the way you hand over a security.
senses.whyCN: 动词是从名词长出来的：to pledge 就是把你的话交出去，方式正如交出一件担保物。

senses.title: To give something as security
senses.definition: to hand over an object or property as a guarantee for a loan
senses.definitionCN: 把物件或财产交出，作为借款的担保
senses.example: She pledged her house to raise money for the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 她抵押了房子，为诊所筹钱。
senses.why: Since the noun named the security itself, the verb could name the act of depositing it, which is why finance keeps this concrete sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词指的就是担保物本身，动词自然可以指「把它交出去」这个动作，所以金融语境里这个具体义项一直活着。

intro.en: Pledge entered English through French as a legal word for a surety, and it is generally thought to go back to a Germanic root rather than to Latin.
intro.cn: pledge 作为法律用语经法语进入英语，本义是「担保」；一般认为它源自日耳曼词根，而非拉丁语。

items.en: Old French plege meant a surety, both the promise and the person or object standing behind it.
items.cn: 古法语 plege 意为担保，既指承诺，也指为承诺作保的人或物。

items.en: The word is generally thought to come from a reconstructed Frankish form plegan, meaning to stand surety; the asterisk marks a form not directly recorded.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词来自法兰克语的重构形式 plegan，义为「担保、负责」；带星号表示这是重构而非直接见于文献的形式。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word into law and trade, where a pledge could be a hostage, a deposit or a formal promise.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个词用于法律与交易，pledge 可以是人质、押金，也可以是正式承诺。

items.en: The sense widened from property to conduct, so people began to pledge loyalty, support and good behaviour.
items.cn: 词义从财物扩展到行为，于是人们开始 pledge 忠诚、支持与良好表现。

items.en: Modern English keeps the legal deposit sense and the public promise sense side by side, from pawnshops to election campaigns.
items.cn: 现代英语让「抵押」与「公开承诺」两个义项并存，从当铺一直用到竞选。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers guarantee words built on the same French or Germanic stock; the near-meaning group gathers words for promises and security.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一法语或日耳曼语来源上的担保类词；近义组收表示承诺与担保的词。

entries.definition: The Old French form from which the English word descends.
entries.definitionCN: 英语词所由来的古法语形式。

entries.definition: To beg or argue a case in court; it looks close but comes from a different Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 恳求；在法庭上申辩。只是拼写相近，词源来自另一个拉丁名词。

entries.definition: The person who receives a pledge as security.
entries.definitionCN: 接受质押物的一方。

entries.definition: The person who gives property as security.
entries.definitionCN: 交出财产作担保的一方。

entries.definition: A statement that you will certainly do something.
entries.definitionCN: 表示一定会做某事的说法。

entries.definition: A very solemn promise, often religious.
entries.definitionCN: 极郑重的誓言，常带宗教色彩。

entries.definition: A firm assurance that something will happen or work.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事会发生或有效的明确保证。

entries.definition: Money or an item left as security.
entries.definitionCN: 作为担保留下的钱或物。

entries.definition: Property promised to a lender if a loan is not repaid.
entries.definitionCN: 借款不能偿还时交给贷方的抵押财产。

normalIntro.en: The word began as the object held against a debt and grew into the spoken promise that carries the same weight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初指被扣下抵债的物件，后来长成同样有分量的口头承诺。

normal.en: A pledge was first a thing left with someone, so the physical image of handing something over is still inside the word.
normal.cn: pledge 最早是留在别人手里的东西，所以「把东西交出去」这个具体画面至今仍藏在词里。

normal.en: Make a pledge uses the noun pattern, while pledge to do uses the verb pattern, and both keep the idea of a binding word.
normal.cn: make a pledge 走名词结构，pledge to do 走动词结构，两者都保留了「话一出口就有约束力」的意思。

normal.en: Election pledge shows the word in public politics, where a promise is made to be judged by voters.
normal.cn: election pledge 把这个词放进公共政治，那里的承诺说出口就是为了让选民日后检验。

normal.en: Pledge oneself to adds a reflexive object, stressing that the speaker personally takes on the duty.
normal.cn: pledge oneself to 加了反身宾语，强调说话人本人把这副担子接了下来。

normal.en: The legal pair pledgee and pledgor splits the two sides of the same security arrangement.
normal.cn: 法律上成对的 pledgee 与 pledgor 把同一项担保安排的两端分开了。

abstract.en: A word for a held object turning into a word for a spoken promise shows how much of trust is about having something at stake.
abstract.cn: 一个指「被扣下的物件」的词转成指「说出的话」，说明信任很大程度上取决于有没有东西押在那里。

abstract.en: Every pledge creates a future that other people are allowed to expect.
abstract.cn: 每一次承诺都造出一个别人有权期待的将来。

abstract.en: The same word covers a pawned watch and a campaign promise because both are securities offered against doubt.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指当掉的手表也指竞选承诺，因为两者都是用来对付怀疑的担保。

examples.en: The government broke its pledge to protect the forest.
examples.cn: 政府违背了保护这片森林的承诺。

examples.en: He left his watch as a pledge for the loan.
examples.cn: 他把手表留下作为这笔借款的抵押。

examples.en: The company pledged to cut its emissions by half.
examples.cn: 这家公司承诺把排放量削减一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑莱吉」——把东西扑到对方手里压着，就是「抵押」，说出口的那句话也一并压上，就成了「誓言」。

root: 古法语 plege（担保）进入英语；一般认为可上溯到法兰克语重构形式 plegan（担保、负责），属日耳曼来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a guarantee held by someone else; it splits into the object deposited and the solemn word given, each with its own noun and verb use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「交到别人手里的担保」；它分成押出去的实物与说出口的郑重的话，两者又各有名词与动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised right hand beside a written promise that must be kept.
core.cn: 核心意象：举起的右手旁边放着一份必须兑现的承诺书。

branches.en: a candidate reading a promise aloud
branches.cn: 候选人当众念出一项承诺

branches.en: a watch left on a lender's desk
branches.cn: 留在放贷人桌上的手表

branches.en: a whole class raising their hands together
branches.cn: 全班一起举起右手

branches.en: the key to a house handed to a bank
branches.cn: 把房门钥匙交给银行

branches.en: a written promise signed in front of witnesses
branches.cn: 在见证人面前签下的书面承诺

intro.en: There is no secure Latin family behind this word; its parts come from French and Germanic sources, with English suffixes building the legal pair.
intro.cn: 这个词背后没有可靠的拉丁词族；它的构件来自法语与日耳曼语，再由英语后缀造出法律上一对身份词。

latinIntro.en: A Latin form is sometimes proposed as an intermediate, but it is itself borrowed from Germanic, so no genuine Latin cognate is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 也有人提出过某个拉丁语中间形式，但它本身借自日耳曼语，因此这里不列真正的拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: forming the past and past participle
items.meaningCN: 构成过去式与过去分词

items.meaning: the one who receives a pledge

definition_zh: 推断；推知；推论
definition_en: to reach an opinion or conclusion from evidence rather than from direct statement
core_image: 几块拼图凑在一起，缺的那一角自动显现
scene: 侦探看着地上一串湿脚印。 From the wet footprints we can infer that someone came in during the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 infer 是「推断」（第 1 个义项：根据证据推出结论）；句意是我们能从湿脚印推断出有人在下雨时进来过。

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ence，义为「推断；推论」
加 -ial，义为「推论的」
加 -able，义为「可推断的」
同出拉丁 ferre，义为「商议；授予」，前缀不同

senses.title: To work out a conclusion
senses.definition: to form a conclusion using the facts you have
senses.definitionCN: 利用已有的事实得出一个结论
senses.example: From the empty cup we inferred that he had already left.
senses.exampleCN: 从那个空杯子我们推断他已经走了。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to bring in, and a conclusion is something you bring in from clues.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「带进来」，而结论就是从线索里带进来的东西。

senses.title: To read meaning into words
senses.definition: to understand something that is suggested but not said
senses.definitionCN: 理解被暗示而非明说的内容
senses.example: I infer from your silence that you disagree.
senses.exampleCN: 从你的沉默里我揣摩出你并不同意。
senses.why: What is not spoken still carries meaning, and the reader must carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 没有说出口的话也带含义，听话的人要把它带出来。

senses.title: To deduce in logic
senses.definition: to move from premises to a necessary conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 从前提出发推出必然的结论
senses.example: From these two rules we can infer the third.
senses.exampleCN: 由这两条规则我们可以推出第三条。
senses.why: In strict logic the word is the technical name for derivation.
senses.whyCN: 在严格逻辑中，这个词是「推导」的专业名称。

senses.title: To guess indirectly
senses.definition: to make an educated guess rather than a certain judgement
senses.definitionCN: 作有依据的猜测，而非确定的判断
senses.example: We can only infer what she meant by that note.
senses.exampleCN: 我们只能猜她想用那张便条表达什么。
senses.why: Because evidence is often incomplete, the verb also covers careful guessing.
senses.whyCN: 由于证据常常不全，这个动词也包含谨慎的猜测。

intro.en: Infer comes from Latin inferre, to bring in, from in- plus ferre, to carry.
intro.cn: infer 来自拉丁语 inferre（带进来），由 in- 加 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: Inferre meant to bring in or bring upon, built on in- plus ferre, to carry.
items.cn: inferre 意为带入或招致，由 in- 加 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: In logic it meant to bring a conclusion into an argument.
items.cn: 在逻辑中它指把一个结论带入论证。

items.en: The verb passed into French and then into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 这个动词经法语于十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: Infer was long used for both drawing and offering a conclusion.
items.cn: infer 长期兼指推出结论与提出结论。

items.en: Modern usage keeps infer for the listener and imply for the speaker.
items.cn: 现代用法中 infer 归听者，imply 归说者。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the ferre family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of reasoning.
note.cn: 形近组收 ferre 词族；近义组收推理类动词。

entries.definition: A conclusion drawn from evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「推断」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: To discuss, or to grant.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「商议；授予」，同出 ferre。

entries.definition: To carry from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「转移」，同出 ferre。

entries.definition: To reach a conclusion by logic.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「演绎；推断」，偏逻辑推演。

entries.definition: To decide after thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「断定」，是推断的结果动作。

entries.definition: To suggest without saying directly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「暗示」，动作来自说者而非听者。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use ferre, to carry, the doubled r in the endings and the split from imply.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 ferre（携带）、词尾双写 r 以及与 imply 的分工。

normal.en: Ferre means carry, so to infer is to carry a conclusion in from the evidence.
normal.cn: ferre 意为携带，所以 infer 就是从证据里把结论带进来。

normal.en: The past form doubles the r: inferred and inferring.
normal.cn: 过去形式双写 r：inferred 与 inferring。

normal.en: Inference is the noun, and inferential is the adjective of logic.
normal.cn: inference 是名词，inferential 是逻辑意义上的形容词。

normal.en: Infer from is the standard pattern: infer X from Y.
normal.cn: infer from 是标准模式：由 Y 推断出 X。

normal.en: The listener infers, the speaker implies: the arrow points opposite ways.
normal.cn: 听者 infer，说者 imply：箭头方向正好相反。

abstract.en: Inference is the shadow a fact casts into the mind.
abstract.cn: 推断是一个事实投进心里的影子。

abstract.en: To infer is to trust the gap: the missing piece is filled by reason, not by seeing.
abstract.cn: 推断是信任那道缝隙：缺的一块由推理补上，而不是由眼睛看到。

abstract.en: The word carries something in, and what it carries is a small act of belief.
abstract.cn: 这个词是把某种东西带进来，而带进来的是一个微小的信念行为。

examples.en: We can infer from his tone that he is angry.
examples.cn: 从他的语气我们可以推断他生气了。

examples.en: Nothing can be inferred from a single case.
examples.cn: 单凭一个案例什么都推断不出来。

examples.en: Readers are left to infer the ending for themselves.
examples.cn: 读者要自己推断出结局。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因佛」——因为拜佛求签，人要自己推断签上的意思。

root: 拉丁语 inferre（带入）= in-（进入）+ ferre（携带）；同族词有 inference、confer、transfer。

sensesIntro.en: From carrying a conclusion in, infer covers reading unspoken meaning, formal logical derivation and cautious guessing when evidence is thin.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把结论带进来」出发，infer 涵盖揣摩言外之意、形式逻辑的推导，以及证据不足时的谨慎猜测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last piece sliding into a jigsaw puzzle.
core.cn: 核心意象：最后一块拼图滑入缺口。

branches.en: CLUE LINE: facts lead to a conclusion.
branches.cn: 线索线：事实导向结论。

branches.en: SILENCE LINE: unspoken meaning is read out.
branches.cn: 沉默线：言外之意被读出来。

branches.en: LOGIC LINE: premises yield a necessary result.
branches.cn: 逻辑线：前提推出必然结果。

branches.en: GUESS LINE: the evidence is not enough.
branches.cn: 猜测线：证据并不充分。

branches.en: MOVEMENT LINE: something is carried in from outside.
branches.cn: 移动线：有东西从外面被带进来。

intro.en: A Latin verb of carrying, which builds a large family of English words with different prefixes.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「携带」动词，用不同前缀造出了大量英语词。

latinIntro.en: The root ferre, to carry, appears in transfer, refer, offer and many other words.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 ferre（携带）出现在 transfer、refer、offer 等大量词中。

definition_zh: 第四十；四十分之一
definition_en: coming after the thirty-ninth, or one of forty equal parts
core_image: 日历翻到第四十页，数字四十被红笔圈出
scene: 这是他第四十次来访。 This is his fortieth visit.
sceneCN: 这里 fortieth 是「第四十」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这是他第四十次来访。

derivatives.zh: 四十
四十年代

senses.title: The ordinal number
senses.definition: coming after thirty-nine in order
senses.definitionCN: 在顺序上位于第三十九之后
senses.example: This is his fortieth visit.
senses.exampleCN: 这是他第四十次来访。
senses.why: This is the main ordinal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的序数义项。

senses.title: One of forty parts
senses.definition: one of forty equal parts of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物被分成四十等份中的一份
senses.example: A fortieth of the land is forest.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地的四十分之一是森林。
senses.why: Ordinals also name fractions.
senses.whyCN: 序数词也可以表示分数。

senses.title: Fortieth in rank
senses.definition: the person or thing in fortieth position
senses.definitionCN: 排在第四十位的人或物
senses.example: She finished fortieth in the race.
senses.exampleCN: 她在比赛中获得第四十名。
senses.why: Ranking uses the same form.
senses.whyCN: 排名也使用同一形式。

intro.en: Fortieth is forty plus the old ordinal ending -th.
intro.cn: fortieth 就是 forty 加上古老的序数后缀 -th。

items.en: Feowertigoða meant fortieth.
items.cn: feowertigoða 意为第四十。

items.en: The form moved toward fortieth.
items.cn: 词形逐渐向 fortieth 演变。

items.en: Fortieth settled as the standard spelling.
items.cn: fortieth 固定为标准拼写。

items.en: It named ranks and anniversaries.
items.cn: 它用来表示名次和周年。

items.en: It also named a fraction.
items.cn: 它也用来表示分数。

note.en: Fortieth is compared with similar-looking words and with other number words.
note.cn: 把 fortieth 与形近词以及其他数词作比较。

entries.definition: coming after the third
entries.definitionCN: 第四

entries.definition: the number 14
entries.definitionCN: 十四

entries.definition: the number 40
entries.definitionCN: 四十

entries.definition: a part of a whole number
entries.definitionCN: 分数

entries.definition: a number that shows order
entries.definitionCN: 序数词

entries.definition: a date remembered each year
entries.definitionCN: 周年纪念

normalIntro.en: Fortieth marks the place where thirty-nine steps end.
normalIntro.cn: fortieth 标出三十九步走完后的位置。

normal.en: This is his fortieth visit.
normal.cn: 这是他第四十次来访。

normal.en: A fortieth of the land is forest.
normal.cn: 这片土地的四十分之一是森林。

normal.en: She finished fortieth in the race.
normal.cn: 她在比赛中获得第四十名。

normal.en: They celebrated their fortieth anniversary.
normal.cn: 他们庆祝了四十周年。

normal.en: His fortieth birthday fell on a Sunday.
normal.cn: 他的四十岁生日是个星期天。

abstract.en: A fortieth is a small piece of a large whole.
abstract.cn: 四十分之一是大整体中的一小块。

abstract.en: Numbers mark time the way stones mark a road.
abstract.cn: 数字标记时间，就像石头标记道路。

abstract.en: The fortieth step can feel like the first.
abstract.cn: 第四十步也可能像第一步。

examples.en: This is his fortieth visit.
examples.cn: 这是他第四十次来访。

examples.en: They celebrated their fortieth anniversary.
examples.cn: 他们庆祝了四十周年。

examples.en: A fortieth of the land is forest.
examples.cn: 这片土地的四十分之一是森林。

dict_mnemonic.text: fortieth 是 forty 加 -th：四十后面的那个位置，就是第四十；把整体分成四十份，一份就是四十分之一。

root: 由 forty（四十）加序数后缀 -th 构成，核心义「排在第四十位或整体的四十分之一」。

sensesIntro.en: Fortieth means the ordinal number after thirty-ninth, a fortieth part, or fortieth in rank.
sensesIntro.cn: fortieth 意为第四十、四十分之一或第四十名。

core.en: The position reached after thirty-nine steps.
core.cn: 走过三十九步后到达的位置。

branches.en: The order reaches number forty.
branches.cn: 顺序数到四十。

branches.en: The whole is split into forty parts.
branches.cn: 整体被分成四十份。

branches.en: A runner holds the fortieth place.
branches.cn: 一名跑者排在第四十位。

branches.en: Counting and ranking share the ordinal.
branches.cn: 计数与排名共享这个序数词。

branches.en: The same ending marks order and fraction.
branches.cn: 同一个后缀既标记顺序也标记分数。

intro.en: Fortieth belongs to the family of number words around forty.
intro.cn: fortieth 属于围绕 forty 的数词家族。

latinIntro.en: Fortieth is Germanic; Latin quadragesimus, fortieth, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: fortieth 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 quadragesimus（第四十）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 两个四十分之一等于一个二十分之一。

items.example: He wrote it in his forties.
items.exampleCN: 他在四十多岁时写了它。

items.example: He lives on the fourth floor.

items.exampleCN: 她的四十岁生日过得很安静。

items.meaning: the fortieth yearly return of a date
items.example: The school held its fortieth anniversary.
items.exampleCN: 学校举办了四十周年庆典。

definition_zh: 追上；超过；突然降临；压倒
definition_en: to catch up with and pass something moving ahead, to become greater than a rival or a figure, and to come upon someone suddenly
core_image: 后视镜里的车影越变越大，最后从侧旁滑到前方
scene: 雨夜的高速路上，一辆货车从后视镜里越来越大。 On the wet highway, the truck pulled out and overtook the slow bus.
sceneCN: 这里 overtake 是「追上并超过」（第 1 个义项：同向赶超前方车辆）；句意为在湿滑的高速公路上，货车变道超过了那辆慢吞吞的巴士。图中可辨识物件：雨夜车灯、后视镜、慢行的巴士。

collocations.zh: 被突发事件赶超；形势令人措手不及

derivatives.zh: 由 overtake 加 -ing 构成，指超过前方车辆的动作，也可放在名词前作定语
overtake 的不规则过去式，表示已经完成的一次赶超

senses.title: To catch up with and pass a moving thing
senses.titleCN: 追上并超过（前方移动的人或车）
senses.definition: to reach the same point as a person or vehicle ahead and then move past it
senses.definitionCN: 赶上前方行进的人或车辆，到达同一点后再越过它
senses.example: The red bus overtook three lorries on the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆红色巴士在山路上超过了三辆卡车。
senses.why: The word joins over, meaning across or beyond, with take, so its first sense is literally taking yourself across the path of what was ahead.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示「越过、在上方」的 over 与 take 组合，字面就是把自己带过前方那辆车所在的位置，所以第一义是同向赶超。

senses.title: To become greater or more successful than
senses.definition: to become larger in amount, or more successful, than someone or something else
senses.definitionCN: 在数量上变得更大，或在成就上变得更强，超过别人或旧有水平
senses.example: Online sales have overtaken those in the high street.
senses.exampleCN: 线上销售额已经超过了商业街实体店的销售额。
senses.why: Once over marks a line being crossed, the same picture fits a chart: one curve climbs past another, and the word needs no new machinery.
senses.whyCN: over 一旦表示跨过某条线，同一幅画面就能搬到图表上：一条曲线爬升到另一条之上，词义从空间顺理成章地扩到数量与地位。

senses.title: To come upon someone suddenly
senses.definition: of a storm, night, illness or event, to reach someone suddenly and without warning
senses.definitionCN: 指风暴、黑夜、疾病或事件毫无预兆地来到某人身上
senses.example: Night overtook the climbers before they reached the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者还没登上山脊，夜色就突然笼罩了他们。
senses.why: Something faster than you can overtake you from behind; the word keeps that racing image when darkness or misfortune arrives sooner than expected.
senses.whyCN: 比人走得更快的东西会从后面赶上人；当黑暗或灾祸比预想更早到来时，这个词保留了那种被追上、被盖过的赛跑画面。

senses.title: To overwhelm someone's control
senses.definition: of a feeling or bodily state, to become so strong that a person can no longer resist it
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪或身体状态强烈到让人无法再抵抗
senses.example: He was overtaken by sleep halfway through the film.
senses.exampleCN: 电影看到一半，他就被睡意压倒了。
senses.why: If an event can overtake a traveller, a wave of feeling can do the same inside a person: it catches up, passes the will, and takes over.
senses.whyCN: 既然事件能从外面赶上旅人，一股情绪也能在人心里做同样的事：它追上来，越过意志，接管了身体。

intro.en: Overtake is an English compound of over and take, recorded in the sense of catching up with someone in the sixteenth century; both parts are native Old English words, not Latin borrowings.
intro.cn: overtake 是 over 与 take 的英语复合词，十六世纪已有「赶上某人」的用法；两个部件都来自古英语本土词，不是拉丁语借词。

items.en: The ancestors are the Old English words ofer, meaning over or across, and tacan, meaning to seize or grasp.
items.cn: 源头是古英语 ofer（在上、越过）与 tacan（抓住、拿取）。

items.en: The two words were already used together in ordinary speech, but the modern spelling of the compound had not yet settled.
items.cn: 两个词在中古英语口语里已经常连用，只是现代拼写尚未定型。

items.en: Writers record overtake first for catching up with a rider or a runner on the road, a purely physical race.
items.cn: 十六世纪的文字里，overtake 先指在路上赶上骑手或奔跑者，是纯粹的身体竞速。

items.en: As trade and transport grew, the word was applied to ships, figures and rivals, so passing became surpassing.
items.cn: 随着贸易与运输发展，词义被用到船只、数字和对手身上，「越过」也就成了「超越」。

items.en: Modern English keeps the irregular overtook and overtaken, and adds the weather sense of being overtaken by night or a storm.
items.cn: 现代英语保留不规则变形 overtook 与 overtaken，并增加了被夜色或风暴突然笼罩的天气义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the other take compounds; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for passing and beating in a race or a ranking.
note.cn: 形近组收其他含 take 的复合词；近义组收在赛道或排名上超过、胜过的动词。

entries.definition: A noun for the act of taking control of a company; the parts are the same but the order is reversed.
entries.definitionCN: 接管、收购一家公司的名词；部件与 overtake 相同，顺序相反。

entries.definition: To agree to do a task and begin it; it shares the take element.
entries.definitionCN: 同意承担并开始做某项任务；与 overtake 共享 take 这一部件。

entries.definition: To get hold of something or move it to another place.
entries.definitionCN: 拿到某物，或把它移到别处。

entries.definition: To go past a person or thing moving in the same direction.
entries.definitionCN: 同向经过某人或某物。

entries.definition: To become better or greater than someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 变得比某人或某物更好或更强。

entries.definition: To be greater than a number or limit.
entries.definitionCN: 大于某个数量或限度。

entries.definition: To reach the same level as someone who is ahead.
entries.definitionCN: 达到与前方某人相同的水平。

normalIntro.en: The word is a plain English compound, and every sense can be seen as one thing moving across the path of another.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是朴素的英语复合词，每个义项都可以看成一样东西越过另一样东西的路线。

normal.en: Over means across, take means to take yourself; overtake is to take yourself across the path of the car in front.
normal.cn: over 是越过，take 是把自己带到，overtake 就是把自己带到前面那辆车的路线上。

normal.en: The past forms are irregular: overtake becomes overtook, then overtaken, like take, took and taken.
normal.cn: 过去式不规则：overtake 变 overtook，再变 overtaken，和 take、took、taken 走同一条路。

normal.en: A takeover reverses the same two parts and names the act of seizing control of a company.
normal.cn: takeover 把这两个部件调换顺序，指夺取一家公司的控制权。

normal.en: In British traffic talk the overtaking lane is the one used to pass slower cars.
normal.cn: 英式交通说法里，overtaking lane 就是用来超过慢车的车道。

normal.en: Being overtaken by night is the same race image moved into the sky.
normal.cn: be overtaken by night 是把同一幅赛跑画面搬到了天上。

abstract.en: Speed turns space into advantage: what was behind you becomes what you leave behind.
abstract.cn: 速度把空间变成优势：原本在你身后的东西，变成被你留在身后的东西。

abstract.en: A curve crossing another curve on a chart is an overtaking with no wheels at all.
abstract.cn: 图表上一条曲线穿过另一条，是一次没有车轮的 overtake。

abstract.en: Anything that arrives faster than you expect has, in the language's eye, simply run past you.
abstract.cn: 任何比你预想更早到来的东西，在语言的眼里都只是从你身旁跑到了前面。

examples.en: The red bus overtook three lorries on the mountain road.
examples.cn: 那辆红色巴士在山路上超过了三辆卡车。

examples.en: Online sales have overtaken those in the high street.
examples.cn: 线上销售额已经超过了商业街实体店的销售额。

examples.en: Night overtook the climbers before they reached the ridge.
examples.cn: 登山者还没登上山脊，夜色就突然笼罩了他们。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃太克」——听成「欧了，我还得再快一点」，超车时喊一声，记住 overtake 是超过。

root: 英语本土复合词：over（越过、在上）加 take（拿、带）；没有直接对应的拉丁同族词，同族词多为 take 的复合形式。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is passing something ahead; the senses then move from road traffic to rankings, to sudden nightfall, and finally to feelings that take control.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是越过前方之物；义项从道路上的超车，延伸到排名上的超越、夜色的突然降临，最后是接管身心的强烈感受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a car growing larger in the mirror, sliding past, and settling in front.
core.cn: 核心意象：后视镜里的车越来越大，从旁边滑过，最后稳稳落在前头。

branches.en: a car sliding past a slower bus in the rain
branches.cn: 雨中一辆车从慢巴士旁滑过

branches.en: a chart line climbing above the old record
branches.cn: 一条曲线爬过旧纪录

branches.en: a young runner beating a veteran champion
branches.cn: 年轻选手击败老冠军

branches.en: night falling on climbers still below the ridge
branches.cn: 夜色落在还没上山脊的登山者身上

branches.en: a passenger nodding off before the film ends
branches.cn: 乘客没等电影结束就睡着了

intro.en: The word is built from two Old English pieces and then carried by later compounds of take; the structure is English, not Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个古英语部件构成，后来又被一系列含 take 的复合词延续；结构属于英语，不属于拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; both of its parts are native Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它的两个部件都来自古英语本土词。

items.meaning: the act of passing a vehicle

definition_zh: 持续时间；期间；音长
definition_en: the length of time that something continues, the period during which it happens, or the length of a sound
core_image: 一只沙漏，沙粒从上格漏到下格，量出一段有多长
scene: 手术室外的走廊里，家属盯着墙上的钟，秒针一圈圈过去。 The duration of the operation was about four hours.
sceneCN: 这里 duration 是「持续时间」（第 1 个义项：某事从开始到结束所经过的时间）；句意是手术持续了大约四个小时。

pos.zh: 名词：持续时间；期间；音长

derivatives.zh: 与 duration 同出拉丁语 durare，义为「耐用的；持久的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「持续时间的；时长的」
由本词同源词加 -ive 构成，义为「持续性的（语法术语）」

senses.title: Length of time
senses.definition: the length of time that something continues or is expected to continue
senses.definitionCN: 某事物持续或预期持续的时间长度
senses.example: The duration of the operation was about four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 手术持续了大约四个小时。
senses.why: Latin durare meant to last, and -ation turns that lasting into a measurable quantity, like sand in a glass.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 durare 意为「持续」，-ation 把这种持续变成一个可测量的量，像玻璃里的沙。

senses.title: A particular period
senses.definition: the period during which something happens, especially a war, a course or a contract
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的整段时间，尤指战争、课程或合同
senses.example: She stayed for the duration of the conference.
senses.exampleCN: 会议期间她一直留在那里。
senses.why: The measured length also names the stretch of time itself, so duration can mean the whole period covered.
senses.whyCN: 被测量出的长度也可以指那段时间本身，所以 duration 也能表示整个覆盖的时期。

senses.title: Length of a sound
senses.definition: the amount of time a speech sound or musical note is held, used in phonetics and music
senses.definitionCN: 语音或音符被持续的时间，用于语音学与音乐
senses.example: In this language, vowel duration can change the meaning of a word.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种语言里，元音的音长能改变词义。
senses.why: Phonetics borrowed the general word because a held sound is simply a duration that can be measured on a machine.
senses.whyCN: 语音学借用了这个通用词，因为一个被拉长的声音就是一段可以在仪器上量出的时长。

intro.en: Duration comes from Latin duratio, a lasting, which was built on durare, to last, and entered English through French.
intro.cn: duration 来自拉丁语 duratio（持续），由 durare（持续）构成，经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Latin durus meant hard or firm, and from it came the idea of holding out or lasting.
items.cn: 拉丁语 durus 意为「坚硬、结实」，由此产生「撑住、持续」的观念。

items.en: The verb durare meant to last or to endure, and it is the direct root of the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 durare 意为「持续、忍耐」，是整个词族的直接词根。

items.en: The noun duratio named the act or state of lasting, and it is the direct source of duration.
items.cn: 名词 duratio 指「持续」的动作或状态，是 duration 的直接来源。

items.en: A French form of the Latin noun carried it toward English, where the spelling settled as duration.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词的法语形式把它带向英语，拼写最终固定为 duration。

items.en: The word is recorded in English by the late fourteenth century, first in learned and legal writing.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪晚期见于英语，最初用于学术和法律文本。

items.en: Everyday use added for the duration, while phonetics and music kept the technical sense of held length.
items.cn: 日常用法增加了 for the duration 这一短语，语音学与音乐则保留了「拉长的时间」这一技术义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin lasting root; the near-meaning group separates length, period, term and span by what they measure.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「持续」词族的词；近义组按所测量的对象区分 length、period、term 与 span。

entries.definition: Able to last a long time; it describes the object, while duration measures the time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「耐用的、持久的」，描述物体本身，而 duration 测量的是时间。

entries.definition: Throughout or within a period; it began as 'while lasting' from the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……期间」，最初由同一动词的「当其持续时」演变而来。

entries.definition: Relating to duration or length of time; duration plus -al.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「持续时间的、时长的」，由 duration 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: To last through difficulty or to bear it; related through Latin durus.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「忍受、持续」，经由拉丁语 durus 同源。

entries.definition: The measured extent of time or space; more general than duration.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「长度、时长」，比 duration 更通用。

entries.definition: A stretch of time with a beginning and an end; it can also name an era.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时期、阶段」，有始有终，也可指一个时代。

entries.definition: A fixed length of time, as of a contract, school year or office; it stresses the limit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「期限、任期」，强调固定的时限。

entries.definition: The full extent from beginning to end, as of a life or a bridge; it stresses the whole reach.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「跨度、全程」，强调从始到终的整体范围。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie duration to the Latin verb for lasting and to the image of sand running through a glass.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 duration 连到表示「持续」的拉丁动词，以及沙粒流过沙漏的画面。

normal.en: durare is to last; duration is the amount of lasting measured out.
normal.cn: durare 是「持续」，duration 就是量出来的持续长度。

normal.en: The suffix -ation turns the verb into a noun of process and result.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ation 把动词变成表示过程与结果的名词。

normal.en: The same root gives durable, during and endure, so the family all points at time.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 durable、during 与 endure，这一族都指向时间。

normal.en: For the duration means for the whole time, until the end.
normal.cn: for the duration 意为在整个期间，直到结束。

normal.en: A long vowel has a longer duration than a short one, which is why phonetics uses the word.
normal.cn: 长元音的 duration 比短元音长，所以语音学用这个词。

abstract.en: Picture an hourglass: the amount of sand that has fallen is the duration already spent.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沙漏：已落下的沙量就是已经耗掉的 duration。

abstract.en: Turn the glass over and the same sand becomes a period with a beginning and an end.
abstract.cn: 把沙漏翻转，同一堆沙就变成有始有终的一段时间。

abstract.en: Duration is time made countable, one grain after another.
abstract.cn: duration 是被变得可数的时间，一粒沙接着一粒沙。

examples.en: The duration of the flight is about eleven hours.
examples.cn: 这次飞行的时长约为十一小时。

examples.en: She stayed for the duration of the conference.
examples.cn: 会议期间她一直留在那里。

examples.en: The drug reduces the duration of the illness.
examples.cn: 这种药能缩短病程。

dict_mnemonic.text: dur- 是「持续」，-ation 是名词后缀：duration 就是「持续出来的那段时间」。

root: 来自拉丁语 duratio「持续」，由动词 durare「持续、忍耐」加名词后缀构成，durare 又源于 durus「坚硬的」。经由法语进入英语，十四世纪晚期已有记录；同族词包括 durable、during、endure。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of duration all measure or name a stretch of time: a length, a whole period, or the held length of a sound.
sensesIntro.cn: duration 的三个义项都在测量或命名一段时间：一个长度、一整段时期，或一个声音被拉长的时长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sand running through an hourglass, measuring how long a thing lasts.
core.cn: 核心意象：沙粒流过沙漏，量出某物持续多久。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: the amount of time from start to finish.
branches.cn: 度量线：从开始到结束的时间总量。

branches.en: THE PERIOD: the whole stretch during which an event or contract runs.
branches.cn: 时期线：某一事件或合同持续覆盖的整段时间。

branches.en: THE SOUND: a held vowel or note measured on a machine.
branches.cn: 声音线：在仪器上量出的拉长元音或音符。

branches.en: LENGTH AND PERIOD: one is the number, the other is the stretch it describes.
branches.cn: 长度与时期：一个是数字，另一个是数字所描述的那一段。

branches.en: SMALL AND LARGE SCALES: a war lasts years, a vowel lasts milliseconds, and both are durations.
branches.cn: 大小尺度：战争持续数年，元音持续毫秒，两者都是 duration。

intro.en: Duration is a Latin-derived noun: a verb root plus -ation, with relatives built on -able and -al.
intro.cn: duration 是源自拉丁语的名词：动词词根加 -ation，亲属词则由 -able 与 -al 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin durus, durare, duratio and durabilis are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 durus、durare、duratio、durabilis 均有记录，只有更早的印欧语词根属于重构。

items.example: The root supplies the sense of holding out.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「撑住」的含义。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的直接来源。
它把 durare 变成 duratio。

items.example: It appears in the English ending -tion.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在英语的 -tion 词尾中。

items.example: It forms during from the old verb dure.
items.exampleCN: 它由旧动词 dure 构成 during。

derivatives.zh: 与 duration 同出拉丁语 durare，义为「耐用的；持久的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「持续时间的；时长的」
由本词同源词加 -ive 构成，义为「持续性的（语法术语）」

definition_zh: 虽然；尽管
definition_en: although, used to introduce a phrase that admits something while qualifying the main statement
core_image: 一句话说完，又回头补上一句「虽然如此」，把话说得更稳
scene: 方案被改得只剩三页，讨论却还没开始。 The plan was accepted, albeit with several conditions.
sceneCN: 这里 albeit 是「虽然、尽管」（第 1 个义项：引导让步短语，表示前面的话要打个折扣）；句意为方案被接受了，尽管附有几个条件。图中可辨识物件：三页方案、长桌、批注笔。

derivatives.zh: albeit 的原始三词形式，义为「尽管它是……」
同一构词模式的古旧连词，义为「虽然；然而」

senses.title: Although, before a phrase
senses.definition: although, used chiefly before an adjective, adverb, or prepositional phrase to concede a point
senses.definitionCN: 意为「虽然」，多用于形容词、副词或介词短语之前，表示让步
senses.example: The plan was accepted, albeit with several conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 方案被接受了，尽管附有几个条件。
senses.why: Albeit is a compressed clause, 'all be it', so it can carry only a small phrase: what follows is the thing that 'is' conceded.
senses.whyCN: albeit 是一个压缩的从句「all be it」，所以只能带一个小短语：后面跟的就是被承认「是」的那一点。

senses.title: Although, before a full clause, in older use
senses.titleCN: 虽然（后接完整从句的古旧用法）
senses.definition: in older writing, although, used before a full clause with its own subject and verb
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧的文字中意为「虽然」，后面可以接带主语和动词的完整从句
senses.example: Albeit he was tired, he stayed until the end.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管他很累，还是留到了最后。
senses.why: Because the word still contains 'it', older writers could let a whole clause follow; modern usage prefers although for that job.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词里仍含有 it，旧时作者可以接一整个从句；现代用法则把这个任务交给 although。

intro.en: Albeit is a whole clause worn down into one word: 'all be it' became a single concessive conjunction.
intro.cn: albeit 是一整个从句磨损成一个词：「all be it」变成了单一的让步连词。

items.en: The phrase all be it meant 'though it be all (that)', a concessive clause used after a statement.
items.cn: 短语 all be it 意为「尽管它是这样」，是放在陈述之后的让步从句。

items.en: Reduced forms such as al be it appear in the fourteenth century, with al as a variant of all.
items.cn: 十四世纪出现 al be it 这类缩减形式，其中 al 是 all 的变体。

items.en: The three words fuse into albeit, and the new word is felt as a single conjunction.
items.cn: 三个词融合成 albeit，新词被当作一个整体连词来使用。

items.en: Albeit is common in formal prose, often introducing a short phrase rather than a clause.
items.cn: albeit 在正式散文中常见，多引导短短语而不是完整从句。

items.en: The word survives mainly in careful writing, where its brevity is valued over the plainer although.
items.cn: 这个词主要活在讲究的文字里，人们看重它比 although 更简洁。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same 'be it' pattern; the near-meaning group gathers concessive connectors.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「be it」模式构成的词；近义组收表示让步的连接词。

entries.definition: An archaic conjunction meaning although or nevertheless.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧连词，意为「虽然」或「然而」。

entries.definition: An archaic conjunction meaning provided that.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧连词，意为「只要；倘若」。

entries.definition: The standard conjunction for conceding a fact before the main clause.
entries.definitionCN: 在主句前承认某一事实的标准连词。

entries.definition: A shorter and more informal form of although, also usable at the end of a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: although 更短更口语的形式，也可放在句末。

entries.definition: Used to contrast two facts, more neutral than a concession.
entries.definitionCN: 用于对比两项事实，比让步更中性。

normalIntro.en: Three real words carry it: all, be, and it, worn down into one conjunction.
normalIntro.cn: 三个真实词承载它：all、be、it，磨损成一个连词。

normal.en: Albeit is all be it: say the three words fast and the conjunction appears.
normal.cn: albeit 就是 all be it：把三个词连快说，连词就出来了。

normal.en: Because it contains be, it likes short phrases rather than full clauses.
normal.cn: 因为里面含有 be，它更爱接短短语而不是完整从句。

normal.en: Albeit is one word, never two: no comma inside it.
normal.cn: albeit 是一个词，不是两个：中间不加逗号。

normal.en: Use albeit for a concession you want to keep brief; use although when a clause follows.
normal.cn: 想简短地让一步就用 albeit；后面跟完整从句时用 although。

normal.en: The stress falls at the end: al-BE-it.
normal.cn: 重音落在末尾：al-BE-it。

abstract.en: A three-word clause collapsed into one word shows how grammar compresses repeated thought.
abstract.cn: 三个词的从句缩成一个词，说明语法会压缩反复出现的想法。

abstract.en: Albeit admits a limitation without withdrawing the claim, which is a very precise social move.
abstract.cn: albeit 承认一个限制，却不撤回主张，这是一种非常精确的社交动作。

abstract.en: The word now sounds formal because plain although does the same work more cheaply.
abstract.cn: 这个词如今显得正式，因为朴素的 although 用更低的成本完成了同样的事。

examples.en: The plan was accepted, albeit with several conditions.
examples.cn: 方案被接受了，尽管附有几个条件。

examples.en: He agreed to help, albeit reluctantly.
examples.cn: 他同意帮忙，尽管很不情愿。

examples.en: The team won the match, albeit by a single point.
examples.cn: 球队赢了比赛，尽管只赢了一分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「噢，必特」——噢，必特先生答应了，虽然有点勉强。

root: 源自中古英语短语 all be it「尽管它是」，三个词融合为一个让步连词。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses concede a point; the only difference is how much grammar the word is allowed to carry after it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都在让一步，区别只在于这个词后面能带多少语法成分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence finishes, then a hand goes back to add 'even so' at the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话说完，一只手又回去在边上补一句「即便如此」。

branches.en: a yes followed by a list of conditions
branches.cn: 一个「同意」后面跟着一串条件

branches.en: a slow yes, said with a sigh
branches.cn: 叹着气说出的那个「好」

branches.en: an old sentence with a full clause after it
branches.cn: 后面接着完整从句的旧式句子

branches.en: a page of seventeenth-century prose
branches.cn: 十七世纪散文的一页

branches.en: one concession, now short and now long
branches.cn: 同一个让步，有时短，有时长

intro.en: Three ordinary English words fused into a single conjunction.
intro.cn: 三个普通英语单词融合成一个连词。

latinIntro.en: Every part is native English; there is no Latin layer, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 每个成分都是英语本族词，没有拉丁语层，因此拉丁词条列表为空。

definition_zh: 非；不；不属于……的；反对票；投反对票的人
definition_en: a prefix meaning not or lacking, and also a vote against a proposal or a person who casts such a vote
core_image: 一个贴在词前面的小牌子，上面只写「非」
scene: 站台上方的牌子写着这趟车中途不停，乘客拖着箱子一路小跑。 The non-stop train to the coast leaves at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 non 是「非、不」的前缀用法（第 1 个义项：表示一般的否定）；句意为开往海边的那趟直达快车在黎明出发。图中可辨识物件：站台上方的牌子、拖着的行李箱、还没亮透的天空。

pos.zh: 非；不（构成否定或表示「非……的」复合词）

collocations.zh: 直飞航班；中途不停的航班

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 non- 加 stop 构成，义为「中途不停的；直达的」
由前缀 non- 加 fiction 构成，义为「非虚构作品」
由前缀 non- 加 smoker 构成，义为「不吸烟的人」
由 non- 与 sense 结合，经中古法语进入英语，义为「胡说；荒谬的东西」

senses.title: Used as a prefix to mean not or without
senses.definition: used before nouns and adjectives to mean not, or the absence of the quality named
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词或形容词前，表示「不」或缺少所提到的性质
senses.example: It is a non-stop flight from Shanghai to London.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一班从上海直飞伦敦的航班。
senses.why: Non is the Latin word for not, and English keeps it as a prefix that simply cancels the meaning of whatever word follows.
senses.whyCN: non 是拉丁语里表示「不」的词，英语把它保留为前缀，直接抵消后面那个词的意思。

senses.title: Used as a prefix to mean not belonging to a group
senses.definition: used before a noun for a person or thing that does not belong to the group or hold the role named
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指不属于该群体或不担任该角色的人或事物
senses.example: She is a non-member, so she cannot vote at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她是非会员，所以在会上不能投票。
senses.why: Cancelling a label also cancels membership, so the same prefix slides from a quality to a category.
senses.whyCN: 取消一个标签，也就取消了归属，于是同一个前缀从性质滑向类别。

senses.title: A vote against, or a person who votes against
senses.definition: a vote cast against a proposal, or a person who casts such a vote
senses.definitionCN: 对某项提议投出的反对票，或投这种票的人
senses.example: The motion passed with ten ayes and two nons.
senses.exampleCN: 动议以十票赞成、两票反对获得通过。
senses.why: In a vote the two sides need short labels, so the negator is turned into a noun that stands for the side saying no.
senses.whyCN: 投票时两方都需要简短的名号，这个否定词就干脆变成名词，代表说「不」的一方。

intro.en: Non is Latin for not; English borrowed it as a prefix through Latin and Anglo-French, and later made it a noun for a vote against.
intro.cn: non 是拉丁语中表示「不」的词；英语经拉丁语与盎格鲁-法语把它借作前缀，后来又让它成为指反对票的名词。

items.en: In Latin non was the plain adverb of negation meaning not, used with verbs and short statements.
items.cn: 在拉丁语里，non 是表示否定的普通副词，意为「不」，与动词和简短陈述连用。

items.en: The phrase non est, it is not, shows how one short negator could deny a whole clause.
items.cn: non est（并非如此）这个短语显示，一个简短的否定词就足以否定整个小句。

items.en: English took non- from Latin and Anglo-French in legal and religious phrases such as non obstante.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语和盎格鲁-法语中吸收 non-，用于 non obstante 这类法律与宗教短语。

items.en: The prefix became productive and built neutral words such as non-member and non-resident.
items.cn: 这个前缀变得能产，造出 non-member、non-resident 这类语气中性的词。

items.en: Modern English freely forms non-stop, non-fiction and non-smoker, and also uses non as a noun for a vote against.
items.cn: 现代英语自由地构成 non-stop、non-fiction 与 non-smoker，也用 non 作名词指反对票。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other negators and one word built with the same prefix; the near-meaning group gathers words for opposition and refusal.
note.cn: 形近组收其他否定词，以及一个用同一前缀构成的词；近义组收表示反对与拒绝的词。

entries.definition: The basic English word that denies a noun: no money, no reason.
entries.definitionCN: 最基本的英语否定词，直接否定名词：没钱、没理由。

entries.definition: The adverb that denies a verb or a whole statement.
entries.definitionCN: 否定动词或整个陈述的副词。

entries.definition: Not one; a pronoun that denies a whole group.
entries.definitionCN: 一个也没有；否定整组的代词。

entries.definition: Words or ideas without sense, built with non-.
entries.definitionCN: 由 non- 构成，指没有意义的话或想法。

entries.definition: In opposition to something or someone.
entries.definitionCN: 反对某事或某人；与……相对。

entries.definition: Strongly disagreeing with or resisting something.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈不同意或抵制某事的。

entries.definition: Saying no, or expressing refusal and denial.
entries.definitionCN: 表示否定，或表达拒绝与否定的。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin negator non, and its English life runs from a borrowed prefix to a small noun on the floor of a debating hall.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语否定词 non；它在英语里的经历，从借来的前缀，一直走到议事厅里那个表示反对的小名词。

normal.en: Non is Latin for not, and it is added to the front of a word rather than standing alone in a sentence.
normal.cn: non 在拉丁语里意为「不」，它加在词的前面，而不在句子里单独使用。

normal.en: Most non- compounds keep a hyphen: non-stop, non-fiction, non-smoker.
normal.cn: 多数 non- 复合词保留连字符：non-stop、non-fiction、non-smoker。

normal.en: Unlike un-, non- usually marks a neutral category rather than a judgement, as in non-fiction compared with untrue.
normal.cn: 与 un- 不同，non- 通常标出一个中性的类别，而不是作出评价，比如 non-fiction 与 untrue 的差别。

normal.en: The noun non, plural nons, is a short label for a vote against a motion.
normal.cn: 名词 non 的复数是 nons，是反对某项动议的简短说法。

normal.en: Standing alone, non is pronounced short and never carries a full sentence by itself.
normal.cn: 单独念 non 时声音短促，它本身从不构成一个完整的句子。

abstract.en: A prefix is a small gate placed before a word, and non- is the plainest gate of all: not this.
abstract.cn: 前缀是放在词前面的一道小门，而 non- 是最朴素的一道：不是这个。

abstract.en: The same negator can cancel a quality, a membership or a proposal, because saying no works the same way in all three.
abstract.cn: 同一个否定词能取消一种性质、一个身份或一项提议，因为说「不」在这三种场合作用相同。

abstract.en: Non is the sound of a door being closed before the word has even entered.
abstract.cn: non 是词还没进门，门就先关上的那一声。

examples.en: It is a non-stop flight from Shanghai to London.
examples.cn: 这是一班从上海直飞伦敦的航班。

examples.en: She reads non-fiction instead of novels.
examples.cn: 她读非虚构作品，而不是小说。

examples.en: The motion passed with ten ayes and two nons.
examples.cn: 动议以十票赞成、两票反对获得通过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「弄」——把门一关，说一句「弄不成」，就是「不」；记住 non 表示否定。

root: 拉丁语 non（不）；中古英语经拉丁语与盎格鲁-法语吸收 non-，多用于法律与宗教短语，后成为构词力很强的前缀；名词义「反对票」是较晚的口语用法。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the Latin negator not; the senses then divide into the prefix that excludes a class and the small noun for a vote against.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是拉丁语的否定词「不」；义项由此分出表示类别排除的前缀，以及指反对票的小名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small sign fixed in front of a word, carrying only the word not.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个贴在词前面的小牌子，上面只写「非」。

branches.en: a sign reading not this
branches.cn: 一块写着「不是这个」的牌子

branches.en: a door marked for members only
branches.cn: 一扇只许会员进入的门

branches.en: a hand raised against a motion
branches.cn: 一只反对动议的手

branches.en: a general no and a no of category
branches.cn: 笼统的否定与分类上的排除

branches.en: standing outside a group and voting outside it
branches.cn: 身处群体之外，也投票站在外面

intro.en: The word is the Latin negator non, which English turned into a productive prefix and, more rarely, into a noun for a vote against.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语否定词 non；英语把它变成能产的前缀，也较少见地把它变成指反对票的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin non is the plain negator behind the prefix, and the same language supplied nullus and negare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 non 是这个前缀背后的普通否定词，同一种语言还提供了 nullus 与 negare。

items.meaning: a person who does not smoke
a person who is not a member

definition_zh: 频繁；频率
definition_en: the rate at which something happens or repeats
core_image: 示波器上一条规律起伏的波线
scene: 这条街上的车流频率在傍晚达到最高。 The frequency of traffic on this street peaks in the evening.
sceneCN: 这里 frequency 是「频率」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这条街上的车流频率在傍晚达到最高。

derivatives.zh: 频繁的
频繁地

senses.title: How often something happens
senses.definition: the fact of something happening often
senses.definitionCN: 某事经常发生的事实
senses.example: The frequency of his visits surprised us.
senses.exampleCN: 他来访如此频繁，让我们很吃惊。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of oftenness.
senses.whyCN: 这是「经常程度」的日常义项。

senses.title: The rate of repetition
senses.definition: the number of times something repeats in a given period
senses.definitionCN: 某事物在给定时间内重复的次数
senses.example: The frequency of traffic on this street peaks in the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这条街上的车流频率在傍晚达到最高。
senses.why: The everyday sense becomes a measurable rate.
senses.whyCN: 日常义项变成了可测量的比率。

senses.title: A rate of waves
senses.definition: the rate at which a sound or radio wave repeats
senses.definitionCN: 声波或无线电波重复的速率
senses.example: This radio station uses a low frequency.
senses.exampleCN: 这家电台使用低频率。
senses.why: Physics turns repetition into a wave property.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把重复变成波的属性。

intro.en: Frequency comes from a Latin word meaning crowded or repeated.
intro.cn: frequency 来自拉丁语中表示「拥挤、反复」的词。

items.en: Frequentia meant a crowd or an assembling.
items.cn: frequentia 意为人群或聚集。

items.en: Frequens meant crowded or repeated.
items.cn: frequens 意为拥挤的或反复的。

items.en: English borrowed frequent first.
items.cn: 英语先借入了 frequent。

items.en: Frequency named how often something returns.
items.cn: frequency 指事物重复出现的频繁程度。

items.en: It became a measure in physics.
items.cn: 它成为物理学中的一种量度。

note.en: Frequency is compared with similar-looking words and words for rates.
note.cn: 把 frequency 与形近词以及表示比率的词作比较。

entries.definition: happening often
entries.definitionCN: 频繁的

entries.definition: often
entries.definitionCN: 频繁地

entries.definition: visited often
entries.definitionCN: 常有人去的

entries.definition: a measure over time
entries.definitionCN: 比率

entries.definition: the state of repeating evenly
entries.definitionCN: 规律性

entries.definition: the fact of happening
entries.definitionCN: 发生

normalIntro.en: Frequency counts how often a thing comes back.
normalIntro.cn: frequency 计算事物回来的频繁程度。

normal.en: The frequency of traffic on this street peaks in the evening.
normal.cn: 这条街上的车流频率在傍晚达到最高。

normal.en: The frequency of his visits surprised us.
normal.cn: 他来访如此频繁，让我们很吃惊。

normal.en: This radio station uses a low frequency.
normal.cn: 这家电台使用低频率。

normal.en: The frequency of buses increases at rush hour.
normal.cn: 高峰时段公交班次更频繁。

normal.en: Word frequency helps learners choose what to study.
normal.cn: 词频帮助学习者选择学习内容。

abstract.en: Repetition leaves a rhythm behind.
abstract.cn: 重复会留下节奏。

abstract.en: What returns often becomes familiar.
abstract.cn: 常回来的事物会变得熟悉。

abstract.en: A wave is a promise kept at a steady pace.
abstract.cn: 波是以稳定节拍守住的承诺。

examples.en: The frequency of traffic on this street peaks in the evening.
examples.cn: 这条街上的车流频率在傍晚达到最高。

examples.en: The frequency of buses increases at rush hour.
examples.cn: 高峰时段公交班次更频繁。

examples.en: This radio station uses a low frequency.
examples.cn: 这家电台使用低频率。

dict_mnemonic.text: frequent（频繁的）+ -cy（名词后缀）= frequency；先记住「频繁」，再理解物理学里的「频率」。

root: 源自拉丁语 frequentia（人群、聚集），来自 frequens（拥挤的、反复的），核心义「反复出现的程度」。

sensesIntro.en: Frequency means how often something happens, a rate of repetition, or a wave rate.
sensesIntro.cn: frequency 意为频繁程度、重复频率或波频。

core.en: How often a thing comes around again.
core.cn: 事物再次出现的频繁程度。

branches.en: Visits come more often than expected.
branches.cn: 来访比预想更频繁。

branches.en: Cars pass at a measurable rate.
branches.cn: 车辆以可测量的比率通过。

branches.en: A radio wave repeats at a set pace.
branches.cn: 无线电波以固定节拍重复。

branches.en: Oftenness becomes a number over time.
branches.cn: 「经常」变成一段时间内的数字。

branches.en: Traffic and waves are both counted by repetition.
branches.cn: 车流与波都靠重复来计数。

intro.en: Frequency builds words for repeated action.
intro.cn: frequency 构成表示反复发生的词。

latinIntro.en: Frequency comes from Latin frequentia.
latinIntro.cn: frequency 来自拉丁语 frequentia。

items.example: High frequency sound is hard to hear.
The frequency of use is low.
The device sends on radio frequency.

definition_zh: 较差的；下级的；下方的；下属
definition_en: lower in quality, rank or position than someone or something else
core_image: 同一座楼里，楼下的办公室比楼上简陋
scene: 公司里同一张表，上下两栏对比鲜明。 The cheaper model is clearly inferior to the one above it.
sceneCN: 这里 inferior 是「较差的」（第 1 个义项：质量上不如别的）；句意是那个便宜的型号明显不如它上面那款。

pos.zh: 形容词：较差的；下级的；下方的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ity，义为「低劣；自卑」
反义同源词，义为「较好的；上级的」
加 -ly，义为「较低地」
固定短语，义为「自卑情结」

senses.title: Lower in quality
senses.definition: not as good as something else of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类之中不如别的
senses.example: The copy is inferior to the original in every way.
senses.exampleCN: 这份副本在各方面都不如原件。
senses.why: The Latin comparative means lower, and lower quality is the everyday extension of lower place.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁比较级意为「更低的」，而质量更低就是位置更低的日常延伸。

senses.title: Lower in rank
senses.definition: having a less important position in a group
senses.definitionCN: 在群体中处于较不重要的位置
senses.example: He was careful how he spoke to inferior officers.
senses.exampleCN: 他对下级军官说话很谨慎。
senses.why: Rank is imagined as height, so those below are called inferior.
senses.whyCN: 等级被想象成高度，位于下面的人就被称为 inferior。

senses.title: Physically below
senses.definition: situated lower, as in anatomy
senses.definitionCN: 位置较低，常用于解剖学
senses.example: The inferior vena cava carries blood upward to the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 下腔静脉把血液向上输送回心脏。
senses.why: In anatomy the word keeps its literal Latin sense of below.
senses.whyCN: 在解剖学里，这个词保留了拉丁语「在下面」的本义。

senses.title: A person of lower rank
senses.definition: a person who ranks below another at work
senses.definitionCN: 在工作中级别低于他人的人
senses.example: She treats her inferiors with respect.
senses.exampleCN: 她尊重自己的下属。
senses.why: The adjective used as a noun names the people who rank lower.
senses.whyCN: 形容词作名词，指级别较低的人。

senses.title: Feeling less worthy
senses.definition: feeling that you are worse than others
senses.definitionCN: 觉得自己不如别人
senses.example: Years of comparison left him feeling inferior.
senses.exampleCN: 常年的比较让他感到自卑。
senses.why: A social rank turns inward and becomes a private mood.
senses.whyCN: 社会等级转向内心，就成为私人的情绪。

intro.en: Inferior is the Latin comparative of inferus, below, literally more below, like the lower one of two.
intro.cn: inferior 是拉丁语 inferus（下面的）的比较级，字面即「更靠下的」，如同两者中较低的那个。

items.en: Inferus meant low or below, and its comparative was inferior, lower.
items.cn: inferus 意为低或在下，其比较级为 inferior（更低的）。

items.en: The same family gave infernus, of the underworld, and the English infernal.
items.cn: 同族词还产生了 infernus（冥界的）以及英语 infernal。

items.en: The comparative form came into English through French in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 这个比较级形式在中古时期经法语进入英语。

items.en: Inferior first described place, then rank, then quality.
items.cn: inferior 先描述位置，再描述等级，最后描述质量。

items.en: The phrase inferior to replaced older patterns of comparison.
items.cn: 短语 inferior to 取代了更早的比较说法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds Latin comparatives; the near-meaning group holds words describing lesser quality or rank.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁比较级词；近义组收描述较差质量或较低等级的词。

entries.definition: Higher in quality or rank.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「较好的；上级的」，与 inferior 相对。

entries.definition: The state of being lower.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「低劣；自卑」。

entries.definition: A great fire, or hell.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「烈火；地狱」，同出拉丁 infernus。

entries.definition: Of poorer quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「更差的」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: Lower in rank.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「下级的；下级」，用于组织。

entries.definition: Of mediocre quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「二流的」，强调质量平庸。

normalIntro.en: The hooks build on the Latin comparative -ior and the fixed pair inferior to, with superior as its mirror.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子建立在拉丁比较级 -ior 与固定搭配 inferior to 上，并以 superior 作镜面。

normal.en: The -ior ending marks a Latin comparative, as in superior and senior.
normal.cn: -ior 词尾标示拉丁比较级，如 superior、senior。

normal.en: Inferior always takes to: inferior to this one, never than.
normal.cn: inferior 总是接 to：inferior to this one，而不用 than。

normal.en: Superior is its exact mirror, built on super, above.
normal.cn: superior 是它精确的镜面，建立在 super（在上）之上。

normal.en: Inferiority complex is the psychological phrase for feeling less than others.
normal.cn: inferiority complex 是表示自卑心理的固定搭配。

normal.en: In anatomy the word simply means below, with no judgement at all.
normal.cn: 在解剖学里这个词只表示「在下面」，毫无贬义。

abstract.en: Inferior is altitude turned into judgement: what is low is thought less.
abstract.cn: inferior 是把高度变成了判断：低的就被认为差。

abstract.en: The word compares, it never measures alone; something is always above it.
abstract.cn: 这个词只在比较中存在，它从不单独出现：总有什么在上面。

abstract.en: To feel inferior is to keep a ladder in the mind and stand on a low step.
abstract.cn: 感到自卑就是在心里放一架梯子，然后站在低处。

examples.en: This cloth is inferior to the one we bought last year.
examples.cn: 这种布不如我们去年买的那种。

examples.en: He never spoke harshly to his inferiors.
examples.cn: 他从不对下属恶语相向。

examples.en: The inferior surface of the leaf is paler.
examples.cn: 叶子的下表面颜色更浅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因费里尔」——因为要花费用，里面的东西就显得比较差。

root: 拉丁语 inferus（下面的）的比较级 inferior（更低的），与 superior 相对；同族词有 inferiority、inferno。

sensesIntro.en: The Latin comparative for lower spreads from physical position to rank, then to quality, to the people below you and finally to a private feeling of worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 表示「更低」的拉丁比较级从物理位置扩展到等级，再到质量、比自己级别低的人，最后到内心对自我价值的感受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plain office on the floor below.
core.cn: 核心意象：楼下那间简陋的办公室。

branches.en: QUALITY LINE: not as good as the other.
branches.cn: 质量线：不如另一个。

branches.en: RANK LINE: lower in an organization.
branches.cn: 等级线：在组织中位置较低。

branches.en: POSITION LINE: literally underneath in anatomy.
branches.cn: 位置线：解剖学中字面意义上的下方。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: those who rank below you.
branches.cn: 人群线：级别低于你的人。

branches.en: SELF LINE: comparison turned into self-doubt.
branches.cn: 自我线：比较转化为自我怀疑。

intro.en: A Latin comparative adjective that still carries the -ior ending of its origin.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁比较级形容词，至今保留其来源的 -ior 词尾。

latinIntro.en: The family of inferus also gives infernal and inferno, all built on the idea of below.
latinIntro.cn: inferus 一族还产生 infernal 与 inferno，都建立在「在下」这一观念上。

definition_zh: 肖像；画像；人像照片；人物描绘
definition_en: a painting, drawing or photograph of a person, especially of the face, or a description that captures someone's character
core_image: 一张脸被固定在一个姿势里，眼神却继续朝外看
scene: 摄影棚里，摄影师请她略微转头，让光落在颧骨上。 The photographer asked her to turn slightly so the portrait caught the light.
sceneCN: 这里 portrait 指「人像照片」（第 2 个义项：以相机拍摄的人物肖像）；句意为摄影师请她略微转头，好让这张人像接住光；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 肖像；画像；人像照片；文字描绘；（纸张的）竖幅

derivatives.zh: portray + -al（名词后缀）→ 描绘出的形象；从「再现动作」转到「产出的形象」
portrait + -ist（从业者）→ 肖像画家；从「作品」转到「作者」
portrait + -ure（行为或结果）→ 肖像画艺术；从「单件」转到「整个实践」
self- + portrait → 自画像；从「他人肖像」转到「自我再现」

senses.title: A painted or drawn image of a person
senses.definition: a painting or drawing representing a person, especially the face
senses.definitionCN: 表现一个人、尤以面部为主的绘画或素描
senses.example: The portrait shows a merchant holding a letter.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像画着一位手持信件的商人。
senses.why: Portrait began as a noun from the verb 'to draw forth'; the drawn likeness of a person is the core that all other senses extend.
senses.whyCN: portrait 最初是动词「拉出、描绘」的名词化；一个人的被描绘形象是其余义项所扩展的核心。

senses.title: A photographic likeness
senses.definition: a photograph of a person, usually posed and framed
senses.definitionCN: 通常经过摆拍与取景的人物照片
senses.example: The photographer asked her to turn slightly so the portrait caught the light.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师请她略微转头，好让这张人像接住光。
senses.why: When photography arrived, the old word for a drawn likeness transferred to the camera: the medium changed, the social function did not.
senses.whyCN: 摄影出现后，旧有的「绘制形象」一词转到相机上：媒介变了，社会功能没变。

senses.title: A description in words
senses.definition: a literary description that captures a person's appearance and character
senses.definitionCN: 在文学中捕捉一个人外貌与性格的描写
senses.example: The novel opens with a portrait of the aunt at her piano.
senses.exampleCN: 小说开篇是姑妈坐在钢琴前的一幅文字肖像。
senses.why: The metaphor 'portrait in words' treats language as a surface that can hold a likeness, an extension recorded in the eighteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 「文字中的肖像」这一隐喻把语言当作能承载形象的表面，这一扩展在 18 世纪有记录。

senses.title: A filmic depiction of a place or group
senses.titleCN: 影视对地点或群体的描绘
senses.definition: a film or television work that depicts a place, community or period in depth
senses.definitionCN: 深入描绘一个地点、群体或时期的电影或电视作品
senses.example: The documentary is a portrait of a fishing town in decline.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片是一个衰落渔港的肖像。
senses.why: The sense widens from a person to any subject treated as a character: a place can be given a face by a film.
senses.whyCN: 词义从人扩展到任何被当作角色处理的对象：一部影片可以给一个地方一张脸。

senses.title: The genre in art history
senses.titleCN: 艺术史中的肖像画门类
senses.definition: the genre of portraiture as classified in art history
senses.definitionCN: 艺术史分类中的肖像画门类
senses.example: Portrait was ranked below history painting in the academy.
senses.exampleCN: 在学院体系里，肖像画的等级低于历史画。
senses.why: A kind of work becomes a genre, so the noun can name the category rather than one object.
senses.whyCN: 一类作品会变成一个门类，因此这个名词能命名类别，而非单件作品。

senses.title: A likeness in any medium
senses.titleCN: 任何媒介中的相似形象
senses.definition: a representation of a person's appearance in any medium
senses.definitionCN: 在任何媒介中对一个人外貌的再现
senses.example: The coin bears a portrait in low relief.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚钱币上有浅浮雕肖像。
senses.why: Once the word means 'likeness', the material is free: paint, stone, metal and pixels can all carry a portrait.
senses.whyCN: 一旦词义是「相似形象」，材料就不受限制：颜料、石头、金属与像素都能承载肖像。

senses.title: Vertical page or screen format
senses.definition: the upright orientation of a page, photograph or screen
senses.definitionCN: 页面、照片或屏幕的竖直方向
senses.example: Switch the page to portrait before printing.
senses.exampleCN: 打印前把页面改成竖幅。
senses.why: A portrait painting is typically taller than it is wide, so the format inherited the name of its usual subject.
senses.whyCN: 肖像画通常高大于宽，因此这种版式继承了其常见题材的名称。

senses.title: A sculpted head or bust
senses.definition: a sculpted head or bust representing a person
senses.definitionCN: 表现一个人的雕塑头部或胸像
senses.example: A marble portrait of the founder stands in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 一尊创始人的大理石胸像立在大厅里。
senses.why: Sculpture adopts the word because the aim is still a recognisable person, even when the medium is stone rather than paint.
senses.whyCN: 雕塑采用这个词，因为目标仍是可辨认的个人，即使媒介是石头而非颜料。

intro.en: Portrait came into English in the sixteenth century from French, ultimately from Latin protrahere 'to draw forth'; it is a doublet of portray. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: portrait 于 16 世纪从法语进入英语，最终来自拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」；它与 portray 是同源双重词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Protrahere meant 'to draw forth, drag out, reveal'; it joined pro- 'forth' to trahere 'to draw, drag'.
items.cn: protrahere 意为「拉出、拖出、显露」，由 pro-「向前」与 trahere「拉、拖」组合。

items.en: Old French portraire meant 'to draw, paint, portray', literally 'to trace forth'; medieval Latin also used protrahere for painting.
items.cn: 古法语 portraire 意为「画、描绘」，字面是「向前描出」；中世纪拉丁也用 protrahere 指绘画。

items.en: Old French portret, the past participle of portraire used as a noun, named a drawn or painted figure.
items.cn: 古法语 portret 是 portraire 的过去分词名词化，指被绘制的人物形象。

items.en: English portrait is recorded in the 1560s as 'a figure drawn or painted', a back-formation from portraiture or a direct borrowing from French.
items.cn: 英语 portrait 于 16 世纪 60 年代有记录，指「被绘制的人物形象」，或由 portraiture 逆构，或直接借自法语。

items.en: The sense narrowed to the head and face represented from life, which became the central everyday meaning.
items.cn: 词义收窄到写生表现的头部与面部，这成为日常核心义。

items.en: Photography, film and printing extended the word to camera likenesses, depictions of places and vertical page formats.
items.cn: 摄影、电影与印刷把这个词扩展到相机拍摄的肖像、地点描绘与竖幅版式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words that are constantly confused with portrait; group two holds nouns for likenesses that differ in medium or scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、常与 portrait 混淆的词；第二组是不同媒介或范围的人物再现名词。

entries.definition: The art of making portraits, or portraits collectively; portrait is one work.
entries.definitionCN: 制作肖像的艺术，或肖像总称；portrait 是一件作品。

entries.definition: To depict in a picture or words; portrait is the resulting noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在图画或文字中描绘；portrait 是结果名词。

entries.definition: A painter or photographer who specialises in portraits; the word names the person, not the work.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻肖像的画家或摄影师；这个名词指人，而非作品。

entries.definition: A portrait in which the artist depicts himself or herself; it is a compound of portrait with self.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术家描绘自己的肖像；是 portrait 与 self 的复合词。

entries.definition: The quality of looking like someone, or an image that resembles them; it need not be a formal portrait.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像某人的性质，或相似的形象；不一定是正式肖像。

entries.definition: A general visual representation; portrait specifies that the subject is a person.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指视觉再现；portrait 限定对象是人。

entries.definition: A sculpture of a person's head and shoulders; portrait includes painted, photographed and full-figure works.
entries.definitionCN: 人物头肩部的雕塑；portrait 还包括绘画、摄影与全身作品。

entries.definition: A side view of a face, or a short biographical sketch; a portrait may be frontal or in profile.
entries.definitionCN: 脸的侧面，或简短生平；肖像可以是正面或侧面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin protrahere 'draw forth' gives both portrait and portray.
normal.cn: 拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」同时给出 portrait 与 portray。

normal.en: The noun is a past participle turned into a thing: 'the drawn-out likeness'.
normal.cn: 这个名词是过去分词变成的物件：「被拉出的形象」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: portrait painter, family portrait, portrait mode.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：肖像画家、全家福、竖屏模式。

normal.en: The family runs portrait, portraiture, portraitist, portray and self-portrait.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 portrait、portraiture、portraitist、portray 与 self-portrait。

normal.en: A page taller than wide is in portrait format because portraits usually are.
normal.cn: 高大于宽的页面叫竖幅，因为肖像通常如此。

abstract.en: Picture a face held still while its look continues to move.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被固定住的脸，目光却仍在移动。

abstract.en: Picture a surface that can be paper, canvas, stone or a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一种可以是纸、画布、石头或屏幕的表面。

abstract.en: Picture a likeness that survives the person it shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个比被描绘者活得更久的形象。

examples.en: The portrait was cleaned and the varnish removed.
examples.cn: 这幅肖像经过清洗，清漆被去掉。

examples.en: He wrote a portrait of his father that avoided sentiment.
examples.cn: 他写下一篇避免感伤的父亲肖像。

examples.en: The stamp carries a portrait engraved from a photograph.
examples.cn: 这枚邮票上有一幅依据照片雕刻的肖像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「por（向前）+ trait（拉）」——把人的样子拉出来 → 肖像

root: 拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」（pro- 向前 + trahere 拉）经古法语 portraire、过去分词 portret，16 世纪 60 年代进入英语为 portrait；与 portray 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the drawn face to the photograph, the verbal description, the filmic place, the genre, any likeness, the vertical format and the sculpted bust.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从绘制的脸出发，转到照片、文字描写、影视地点、艺术门类、任何媒介的相似形象、竖幅版式与雕塑胸像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face is fixed in a pose while its gaze keeps looking outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张脸被固定在一个姿势里，目光却继续朝外看。

branches.en: THE LIKENESS IN MATTER: painted or sculpted, both aim at a recognisable person.
branches.cn: 材料中的形象：绘画或雕塑，目标都是可辨认的个人。

branches.en: THE CAMERA: the drawn likeness becomes a photographic one.
branches.cn: 相机：被绘制的形象变成照片。

branches.en: IN WORDS AND ON FILM: a person described, then a place given a face.
branches.cn: 文字与影片：先描写一个人，再给一个地方一张脸。

branches.en: CATEGORY AND MEDIUM: the genre, then any material that can carry it.
branches.cn: 类别与媒介：先是门类，再是任何能承载它的材料。

branches.en: FORMAT: the upright page inherits the shape of its usual subject.
branches.cn: 版式：竖幅页面继承了其常见题材的形状。

intro.en: Portrait is a Latin participle form borrowed through French; its family includes the verb of depicting and the name of the practice.
intro.cn: portrait 是经法语借入的拉丁分词形式；其词族包括描绘动词与指称这门实践的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin protrahere and trahere supply the root; the -trait ending is the French past-participle shape, not a living English suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 protrahere 与 trahere 提供词根；-trait 词尾是法语过去分词形态，不是能产的英语后缀。

items.example: The prefix contributes the sense of drawing out.
Trahere also gives tractor and trace.
items.exampleCN: trahere 还给出 tractor 与 trace。

items.example: The verb passed into English as portray.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词进入英语成为 portray。

items.structure: French portrait, past participle of portraire
items.example: The portrait was hung above the fireplace.
items.exampleCN: 这幅肖像挂在壁炉上方。

items.example: The novel portrays the city in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说描绘冬天的城市。

items.example: The portraitist worked only in pastel.
items.exampleCN: 这位肖像画家只用色粉。

items.example: The self-portrait shows the artist at work.
items.exampleCN: 这幅自画像表现正在作画的艺术家。

definition_zh: 流产；堕胎；人工流产；（计划等的）夭折
definition_en: the ending of a pregnancy, or the failure of a plan before it develops
core_image: 一株刚发芽的苗被移出花盆
scene: 诊所里，医生用平实的语言说明终止妊娠的风险。 The clinic explained the risks of abortion in plain language.
sceneCN: 这里的 abortion 指「人工流产」（第 1 个义项：人为终止妊娠）；句意是诊所把人工流产的风险讲得很明白。

derivatives.zh: 义为「流产；中止」
加 -ive 构成，义为「失败的；夭折的」
义为「中途失败地」

senses.title: The ending of a pregnancy
senses.definition: the ending of a pregnancy before the fetus can survive
senses.definitionCN: 胎儿尚不能存活时妊娠终止
senses.example: The clinic explained the risks of abortion in plain language.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把人工流产的风险讲得很明白。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to miscarry, and the noun names that ending.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「小产」，名词便指这一终止。

senses.title: A medical procedure
senses.definition: a procedure chosen to end a pregnancy
senses.definitionCN: 人为选择终止妊娠的医疗操作
senses.example: The law sets out when an abortion may be performed.
senses.exampleCN: 法律规定何时可以施行人工流产。
senses.why: Once medicine could perform it safely, the word named the procedure itself.
senses.whyCN: 医学能安全施行之后，这个词便指这项手术。

senses.title: A natural loss
senses.definition: in medicine, the body's own loss of a pregnancy
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指身体自行失去妊娠
senses.example: Doctors call this kind of loss a spontaneous abortion.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把这类失去称为自然流产。
senses.why: The oldest medical sense covers any pregnancy that ends early, however it happens.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的医学义涵盖一切提早结束的妊娠，无论原因如何。

senses.title: A plan that fails
senses.definition: the failure of a scheme before it is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 计划在实施之前就失败
senses.example: The project was an abortion from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目从一开始就注定夭折。
senses.why: Something cut off before it can live is the image behind the figurative use.
senses.whyCN: 在能成活之前就被截断，正是这一比喻义的意象。

senses.title: A mission cut short
senses.definition: the stopping of a flight or mission before completion
senses.definitionCN: 飞行或任务在完成前被中止
senses.example: The launch was an abortion after the fuel leak.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料泄漏之后，这次发射成了一次中止。
senses.why: Engineering borrowed the medical word for anything halted before its end.
senses.whyCN: 工程界借用了这个医学词，指任何中途停止之事。

senses.title: A stunted organ
senses.definition: in botany, a part that stops developing
senses.definitionCN: 植物学上指停止发育的部分
senses.example: The flower shows abortion of the stamens.
senses.exampleCN: 这朵花表现出雄蕊发育不全。
senses.why: A part that never reaches full form is a pregnancy that never comes to term.
senses.whyCN: 未能长成的部分，正如未能足月的妊娠。

senses.title: A public controversy
senses.definition: the word used in debates about the legal right to end a pregnancy
senses.definitionCN: 在关于终止妊娠的法律权利辩论中所用的词
senses.example: Abortion remains a central issue in the election.
senses.exampleCN: 堕胎仍是这次选举的核心议题。
senses.why: A medical term becomes a political label when law and morals take it up.
senses.whyCN: 当法律与道德介入，医学词便成了政治标签。

senses.title: An imperfect result
senses.definition: something badly made or left unfinished
senses.definitionCN: 制作粗劣或未完成的事物
senses.example: The report was a rushed abortion of a draft.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是一份草率仓促的稿子。
senses.why: The idea of something born too soon extends to any botched work.
senses.whyCN: 「出生太早」的观念延伸到任何做坏的东西。

intro.en: The word comes from a Latin verb meaning to miscarry.
intro.cn: 这个词出自意为「小产」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: aboriri meant to miscarry, from ab-, away, and oriri, to be born.
items.cn: aboriri 意为「小产」，由 ab-（离开）与 oriri（出生）构成。

items.en: abortio named a miscarriage or an untimely birth.
items.cn: abortio 指小产或不足月的生产。

items.en: abortivus described something born too soon.
items.cn: abortivus 形容出生过早之物。

items.en: avortement carried the medical sense into French.
items.cn: avortement 把这个医学义带进法语。

items.en: abortion first meant an untimely birth.
items.cn: abortion 最初指不足月的生产。

items.en: the medical, legal and figurative senses separated.
items.cn: 医学、法律与比喻三层含义逐渐分开。

note.en: The look-alike group is the abort family; the near-meaning group is medical and general words for early loss.
note.cn: 形近组是 abort 词族；近义组是表示「早期失去」的医学与一般用词。

entries.definitionCN: 使流产；中止

entries.definition: failing before it is complete
entries.definitionCN: 夭折的；失败的

entries.definition: in a way that comes to nothing
entries.definitionCN: 中途失败地

entries.definitionCN: 自然流产

entries.definition: the ending of something, including a pregnancy
entries.definitionCN: 终止（包括终止妊娠）

entries.definition: the birth of a baby that has died
entries.definitionCN: 死产

entries.definition: a lack of success
entries.definitionCN: 失败

normalIntro.en: These hints follow aboriri and the abort family.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条贴着 aboriri 与 abort 词族。

normal.en: oriri means to rise or be born, and ab- turns it away.
normal.cn: oriri 意为「升起、出生」，ab- 把它推向反面。

normal.en: aboriri is literally to be born away, that is, to miscarry.
normal.cn: aboriri 字面是「生偏了」，也就是小产。

normal.en: abortion is the noun, abort is the verb.
normal.cn: abortion 是名词，abort 是动词。

normal.en: abortive describes a plan that never gets going.
normal.cn: abortive 形容从未真正启动的计划。

normal.en: spontaneous abortion is the medical term for a natural loss.
normal.cn: spontaneous abortion 是自然流产的医学术语。

abstract.en: See a seed lifted out before it sprouts.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子还没发芽就被取走。

abstract.en: Picture a launch stopped on the pad.
abstract.cn: 想象发射在发射台上被叫停。

abstract.en: Think of a sentence broken off in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话说到一半被截断。

examples.en: The clinic offers counselling before an abortion.
examples.cn: 诊所在人工流产前提供咨询。

examples.en: The law on abortion varies from country to country.
examples.cn: 各国的堕胎法各不相同。

examples.en: The mission was an abortion after the first failure.
examples.cn: 第一次失败之后，这项任务就夭折了。

sensesIntro.cn: 「过早的出生」长成一项医疗操作、一个公共议题，以及任何做坏的计划。

core.cn: 核心意象：幼芽还没长成就被取出。

branches.cn: 夭折的计划与做坏的东西

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of early birth with an English -ion ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「早产」名词加英语 -ion 词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root oriri, to rise or be born, also gives orient and origin.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 oriri（升起、出生）也生出 orient 与 origin。
