definition_zh: 人类；世人；人间；（旧）男性
definition_en: all human beings considered as one group or species; also, in older usage, men as distinct from women
core_image: 无数张脸叠成同一张脸，站成一条望不到尽头的队伍
scene: 旧书阅览室的窗边，一位读者翻开讨论人类起源的书，页边还夹着一张发黄的星图。 The chapter asked what mankind might become in another thousand years.
sceneCN: 这里 mankind 是「人类（全体）」（第 1 个义项：把人作为一个物种整体来看）；句意为这一章追问人类再过千年会变成什么样子。图中可辨识物件：阅览室的窗、发黄的星图、摊开的厚书。

derivatives.zh: 由 human 与 kind 复合而成，为避开 man 的性别色彩而造的平行词，义为「人类」
出自拉丁语 humanitas（人性、人类），义为「人类；人性；仁慈」
古英语 mann 本指「人」，不分男女，后来收窄为「成年男子」，是同族里最基础的一个

senses.title: The human race as a whole
senses.definition: all human beings taken together as one group or species
senses.definitionCN: 把所有的人作为一个整体或一个物种来看
senses.example: The library holds centuries of writing about mankind's place among the stars.
senses.exampleCN: 这座图书馆收藏着几个世纪以来关于人类在星空中位置的作品。
senses.why: Old English mann meant any human being and cynd meant nature or race, so the compound named the race of people rather than a single person.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mann 指任何一个人、不分男女，cynd 指天性或族类，所以这个复合词命名的是人的族类，而不是某一个人。

senses.title: The mortal world, in literary use
senses.definition: humanity seen as a mortal world set against heaven, nature or eternity
senses.definitionCN: 把人世看作与上天、自然或永恒相对的有死之物
senses.example: The poem asks what mankind can leave behind when the mountains wear away.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗追问：当群山也被磨平时，世人还能留下什么。
senses.why: Once the word names every living person, a poet can put it on one side of a contrast with heaven on the other, and the group becomes the whole mortal scene.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指所有活着的人，诗人就能把它放在对照的一端、让上天站在另一端，于是一群人就变成了整个有死的世间。

senses.title: Men as distinct from women, an older usage
senses.definition: male human beings taken as a group, an older sense now often replaced in careful writing
senses.definitionCN: 把男性作为一个群体来看的旧义项，如今在审慎的文字中常被替换
senses.example: An older dictionary defines the word as the males of the human race.
senses.exampleCN: 一部较早的词典把这个词释义为「人类的男性」。
senses.why: English mann first covered both sexes and later narrowed to the male; readers then reanalysed mankind as men plus kind, and the male-only sense grew out of that split.
senses.whyCN: 英语 mann 原兼指男女，后来收窄为男性；读者于是把 mankind 重新拆成 men 加 kind，男性专指义便从这道裂缝里长出来。

intro.en: Mankind is an Old English compound of two ordinary words, one for a person and one for a race or nature, and its history includes a later narrowing that still troubles careful writers.
intro.cn: mankind 是古英语里由两个普通词拼成的复合词，一个指人，一个指族类或天性；它的历史里还有一次后来的收窄，至今仍让审慎的作者为难。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic noun for a human being stands behind Old English mann; the reconstructed form is generally written manniz.
items.cn: 古英语 mann 背后是一个重构的日耳曼语名词，意为「人」；这个重构形式一般写作 manniz。

items.en: Mann meant a human being of either sex, and the plural menn covered people in general, not men as opposed to women.
items.cn: mann 指不分男女的人，复数 menn 泛指众人，而不是与女性相对的男性。

items.en: Cynd meant nature, family or race, and the related gecynd named an inborn kind or quality.
items.cn: cynd 意为天性、家族或族类，相关的 gecynd 指天生的种类或性质。

items.en: Middle English joined the two words as mankynde, the race of people, and the spelling slowly settled into mankind.
items.cn: 中古英语把两个词合成 mankynde，指人的族类，拼写后来慢慢固定为 mankind。

items.en: Modern English keeps mankind for the species, notes the older male-only sense, and prefers humankind in much formal writing today.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 mankind 指人类这一物种，也记录较早的男性专指义；如今许多正式文字更愿意用 humankind。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the two halves of the compound and its parallel coinages; the near group gathers other names for people taken as a whole.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的两个组成部分及其平行造词；近义组收其他把人们作为整体来称呼的词。

entries.definition: An adult male, or, in older use, a person of either sex.
entries.definitionCN: 成年男子；在较早用法中也指不分男女的人；古英语 mann 是其源头。

entries.definition: A type or sort of thing, from the same Old English word for nature and race.
entries.definitionCN: 事物的种类；出自同一个表示天性与族类的古英语词，是 mankind 的后半部分。

entries.definition: A parallel word for the human race, coined with human to avoid the male colour of man.
entries.definitionCN: 与 mankind 平行的说法，用 human 取代 man 以避开男性色彩。

entries.definition: The state of being an adult male, or the qualities traditionally expected of one.
entries.definitionCN: 成年男子的身份，或传统上要求于男子的品质；由 man 加 -hood 构成。

entries.definition: The human race as a whole, or the quality of being humane.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的人类；也指仁厚的人性。

entries.definition: Human beings in general, or the members of a community.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指人；也指某个群体的成员。

entries.definition: Human beings, named as creatures that must die.
entries.definitionCN: 把人称作必死的造物，属文学用法。

normalIntro.en: The word is two Old English nouns pressed together, and its family keeps returning to the person, the race, and the quarrel over whether the race includes everyone.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是两个古英语名词压在一起，它的同族词反复回到「人」「族类」，以及那场关于族类是否包含所有人的争论。

normal.en: Old English mann meant a human being of either sex, so the first half of the word was never male-only.
normal.cn: 古英语 mann 指不分男女的人，所以这个词的前半部分原本并不专指男性。

normal.en: The second half is cynd, nature or race, the same word that gives English kind and kin.
normal.cn: 后半部分是 cynd，意为天性或族类，也是英语 kind 与 kin 的来源。

normal.en: Put together, the compound literally says the race of human beings, which is why it takes no plural.
normal.cn: 合起来，这个复合词字面说的就是「人的族类」，所以它没有复数形式。

normal.en: Middle English man narrowed towards the male, and readers then heard mankind as men plus kind.
normal.cn: 中古英语里 man 收窄向男性，读者随后就把 mankind 听成 men 加 kind。

normal.en: Humankind was coined later to keep the species sense while dropping the gender burden.
normal.cn: humankind 是后来造出来的，为的是保住「物种」的意思，同时卸掉性别的负担。

abstract.en: One word holds a whole species, yet its first half once meant every person alive.
abstract.cn: 一个词装下整个物种，而它的前半部分曾经指每一个活着的人。

abstract.en: A compound can age: the same letters now sound narrower than they did a thousand years ago.
abstract.cn: 复合词也会变老：同样的字母，如今听起来比千年前窄了许多。

abstract.en: Mankind is a name for everyone, which is exactly why the argument about its edges never quite ends.
abstract.cn: mankind 是给所有人的名字，也正因如此，关于它边界的争论总也停不下来。

examples.en: The library holds centuries of writing about mankind's place among the stars.
examples.cn: 这座图书馆收藏着几个世纪以来关于人类在星空中位置的作品。

examples.en: The poem asks what mankind can leave behind when the mountains wear away.
examples.cn: 这首诗追问：当群山也被磨平时，世人还能留下什么。

examples.en: An older dictionary defines the word as the males of the human race.
examples.cn: 一部较早的词典把这个词释义为「人类的男性」。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「满金」——满世界的金子都属于人类全体；记住 mankind 是人类，是不可数的整体。

root: 古英语 mann（人，不分男女）加 cynd（天性、族类），合成 mankynde，后写作 mankind；mann 可追到原始日耳曼语重构形式 manniz。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a whole species held in one word; the senses then divide into the biological group, the mortal world of literary contrast, and an older male-only reading.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是用一个词装下整个物种；义项由此分成作为物种的人群、文学对照里的有死世间，以及较早的男性专指义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: countless faces folded into one face, standing in a line that has no visible end.
core.cn: 核心意象：无数张脸叠成同一张脸，站成一条望不到头的队伍。

branches.en: a long queue of faces stretching past the horizon
branches.cn: 一长队面孔延伸过地平线

branches.en: an old book open under a library window
branches.cn: 旧书在阅览室的窗下摊开

branches.en: mountain ridges slowly worn down by weather
branches.cn: 山脊被风霜一点点磨低

branches.en: a dictionary entry read aloud in a classroom
branches.cn: 课堂里有人念出一条词典释义

branches.en: two readings of one compound splitting apart
branches.cn: 同一个复合词的两种读法分开

intro.en: Two Old English nouns, one for a person and one for a race, plus their modern relatives and two English formations carry mankind from a plain compound to a contested name for a species.
intro.cn: 两个古英语名词，一个指人、一个指族类，再加上它们的现代同族词与两个英语构词形式，把 mankind 从普通复合词带到一个有争议的物种名称。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this compound; Latin homo means a human being, but it belongs to a different root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；拉丁语 homo 意为「人」，但它建立在另一个词根上。

items.meaning: an adult male, or a person in older use
items.meaningCN: 成年男子；较早用法中也泛指人

items.meaning: the human race, or humane feeling

definition_zh: 坚持不懈的；执着的；持续的；连绵不断的；反复出现的；顽固的；难以消除的；持久性的；长期存续的
definition_en: continuing firmly despite difficulty, or continuing to exist, appear, or remain far longer than expected, whether of a person, a symptom, a smell, a chemical, or stored data
core_image: 那颗按钮被一直按着，所以灯始终亮着，谁也没能把它关掉
scene: 楼道尽头那盏灯坏了三个月还没修，每次经过都还亮着。 The lamp at the end of the hall has been a persistent fault for three months.
sceneCN: 这里 persistent 是「反复出现的、挥之不去的」（第 3 个义项：问题一再出现、始终没有消失）；句意：走廊尽头那盏灯是个持续了三个月的反复故障；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 坚持不懈的；持续的；反复出现的；顽固的；持久性的

derivatives.zh: 坚持；持续存在
坚持不懈；持续存在；持久性
持续地；一再地
持续性（异体）
非持久的；不残留的

senses.title: Refusing to give up
senses.definition: of a person, continuing firmly with an aim despite obstacles, rejection, or repeated failure
senses.definitionCN: 指人面对障碍、拒绝或反复失败仍坚定继续追求目标
senses.example: A persistent student kept coming back until the proof worked.
senses.exampleCN: 一个不肯放弃的学生一次次回来，直到证明走通。
senses.why: Persistent is the present participle of persistere, 'standing thoroughly'. The adjective describes the hand that has not lifted from the button, not the difficulty it faces.
senses.whyCN: persistent 是 persistere“彻底站住”的现在分词。这个形容词描述的是那只还没有离开按钮的手，而不是它面对的困难。

senses.title: Continuing without a break
senses.definition: of a condition, sound, or process, continuing over a long period without stopping
senses.definitionCN: 指状况、声音或过程在长时间内不断持续
senses.example: A persistent hum came from the transformer all night.
senses.exampleCN: 变压器的持续嗡鸣响了一整夜。
senses.why: Here the light simply stays on. No struggle and no praise: the adjective measures duration, and persistent becomes close to continuous.
senses.whyCN: 这里的灯只是持续亮着。没有挣扎也没有赞许：形容词衡量的是时长，persistent 因此接近 continuous。

senses.title: Coming back again and again
senses.definition: of a problem, symptom, rumour, or error, appearing repeatedly and refusing to go away
senses.definitionCN: 指问题、症状、传闻或错误反复出现、不肯消失
senses.example: The persistent leak was traced to a hairline crack.
senses.exampleCN: 这个反复出现的渗漏最终被追查到一条细裂缝。
senses.why: The button is being pressed again each time the fault returns. The adjective marks the repetition, not the length, which is why a persistent cough can be short and a persistent rumour can be old.
senses.whyCN: 每次故障回来，按钮就被再按一次。这个形容词标记的是重复而非长度，所以 persistent 的咳嗽可以很短，persistent 的传闻可以很旧。

senses.title: Hard to remove
senses.definition: of a stain, smell, habit, or stain-like thing, remaining despite attempts to remove or change it
senses.definitionCN: 指污渍、气味或习惯在试图去除或改变之后仍然存在
senses.example: A persistent smell of smoke stayed in the curtains for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘上的烟味挥之不去，持续了好几周。
senses.why: Some lamps cannot be switched off by ordinary means. This sense stresses resistance to cleaning or correction, with the same image of a light that keeps burning.
senses.whyCN: 有些灯用普通办法关不掉。这个义项强调对清洁或纠正的抵抗，意象仍是那盏一直烧着的灯。

senses.title: Remaining in the environment
senses.definition: of a chemical or pollutant, remaining in soil, water, or organisms for a long time without breaking down
senses.definitionCN: 指化学品或污染物在土壤、水体或生物体内长期存在而不分解
senses.example: Persistent pesticides accumulate up the food chain.
senses.exampleCN: 持久性农药会沿食物链逐级累积。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the duration sense and made it a measurable property. The lamp refuses to go out, and the measure of that refusal becomes an environmental warning.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了持续义，并把它变成可测量的属性。灯拒绝熄灭，这种拒绝的程度就成了环境警告。

senses.title: Stored beyond the session
senses.definition: of data or an object in computing, remaining stored after a program, session, or device stops
senses.definitionCN: 指数据或对象在程序、会话或设备停止后仍被保存
senses.example: Persistent storage keeps the user's settings after a reboot.
senses.exampleCN: 持久化存储让用户的设置在重启后仍然保留。
senses.why: Memory loses its light when the power ends; persistent storage is built so the button is held by something slower and more permanent than electricity.
senses.whyCN: 内存断电就失去光；持久化存储的设计让按钮被某种比电更慢、更永久的东西按住。

senses.title: A symptom that will not settle
senses.definition: of a medical sign, infection, or pain, continuing longer than expected or returning after treatment
senses.definitionCN: 指医学体征、感染或疼痛持续超过预期，或治疗之后再次出现
senses.example: Persistent fever for more than a week needs investigation.
senses.exampleCN: 持续一周以上的发热需要进一步检查。
senses.why: The body's lamp stays lit after the illness should have ended. Medicine uses the adjective to separate a passing reaction from a state that has taken up residence.
senses.whyCN: 身体的灯在本该结束之后仍亮着。医学用这个形容词把一时的反应与已经“住下来”的状态分开。

senses.title: Refusing to be put off
senses.definition: of a person's manner, continuing to ask, demand, or appear despite hints that they should stop
senses.definitionCN: 指人的举止，在别人暗示应当停止时仍继续询问、要求或出现
senses.example: The persistent salesman called four times in one week.
senses.exampleCN: 那个纠缠不休的推销员一周打了四次电话。
senses.why: The same standing posture, now seen from the receiving side. Persistence is virtue when you want the goal; persistent is annoying when you are the obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 同一个站立的姿势，现在从被面对的一方来看。当目标是你要的，坚持是美德；当你就是障碍时，persistent 就很烦人。

senses.title: Lasting across generations
senses.definition: of a tradition, belief, species, or pattern, surviving over a very long period despite pressure to disappear
senses.definitionCN: 指传统、信念、物种或模式在消失的压力下仍长期存续
senses.example: The persistent custom survived two centuries of migration.
senses.exampleCN: 这个长存的习俗挺过了两个世纪的迁徙。
senses.why: The largest lamp again: a whole pattern stays lit. Persistent here is measured in generations, and the hand on the button is a community that keeps passing it on.
senses.whyCN: 又是最大的一盏灯：一整套模式持续亮着。这里的 persistent 以世代计量，按住按钮的是不断把它传下去的共同体。

intro.en: Persistent is the English adjective from Latin persistens, the present participle of persistere 'to stand firm, continue'. Persistere is per- 'thoroughly' plus sistere 'to stand'. The adjective entered English in the 16th century, first for persons and opinions, then spreading in the 19th and 20th centuries to symptoms, chemicals, and computer storage.
intro.cn: persistent 是来自拉丁语 persistens 的英语形容词，即 persistere“站稳、持续”的现在分词。persistere 是 per-“彻底”加 sistere“站立”。这个形容词在 16 世纪进入英语，最早用于人与意见，19 至 20 世纪扩展到症状、化学品与计算机存储。

items.en: Sistere 'to stand, to place' comes from the reconstructed PIE form *sta- 'to stand'. The prefix per- 'thoroughly' makes persistere 'to stand through to the end'.
items.cn: sistere“站立、放置”出自原始印欧语的重构形式 *sta-“站立”。前缀 per-“彻底”使 persistere 成为“站到最后”。

items.en: The present participle persistens, persistentem supplies English with both persistent and, through the noun persistentia, persistence. The two words entered English on parallel tracks rather than one from the other.
items.cn: 现在分词 persistens、persistentem 同时为英语提供 persistent 与（经名词 persistentia 的）persistence。这两个词是平行进入英语的，而不是一个由另一个派生。

items.en: English persistent first describes people and opinions that hold their ground. The tone can be admiring or critical depending on the sentence.
items.cn: 英语 persistent 最早描述守住立场的人与意见。语气可褒可贬，取决于句子。

items.en: Medicine and chemistry adopt it for symptoms and substances that stay: persistent fever, persistent odour, persistent dyes.
items.cn: 19 世纪医学与化学用它描述滞留的症状与物质：持续发热、挥之不去的气味、不易褪色的染料。

items.en: Computing adds persistent storage and persistent connections; environmental science fixes the phrase persistent organic pollutants.
items.cn: 20 世纪计算机加入持久化存储与持久连接；环境科学固定了“持久性有机污染物”这一说法。

items.en: Perseverant looks like a twin but comes from perseverare, a different Latin verb. Persistent is the participle of persistere; the two overlap in meaning without sharing a formation.
items.cn: perseverant 看起来像双胞胎，却来自另一个拉丁动词 perseverare。persistent 是 persistere 的分词；两者意义重叠，构词却不同。

note.en: The first group separates the adjective from its noun family and from two near neighbours built differently. The second group compares continual, continuous, stubborn, and lingering.
note.cn: 第一组把形容词与其名词词族分开，并区分两个构词不同的近邻。第二组比较 continual、continuous、stubborn、lingering。

entries.definition: the state of standing firm or continuing. It names the quality; persistent describes the thing that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 站稳或持续的状态。它命名品质，persistent 描述具有该品质的事物。

entries.definition: to continue firmly or keep existing. It is the verb behind the participle.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定继续或持续存在。它是分词背后的动词。

entries.definition: steadfast in a course of action, from Latin perseverare. It overlaps in meaning but is not the participle of persistere.
entries.definitionCN: 在行动道路上坚定不移的，出自拉丁 perseverare。意义重叠，却不是 persistere 的分词。

entries.definition: to stand against. It shares sistere 'stand' but points the posture in the opposite direction.
entries.definitionCN: 站在对立面；抵抗。它共享 sistere“站立”，却把姿势指向相反方向。

entries.definition: happening repeatedly over a period, often with interruptions. It fits a recurring cough or complaint better than an unbroken hum.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时间内反复发生，常有中断。它更适合反复的咳嗽或抱怨，而不是不间断的嗡鸣。

entries.definition: going on without any interruption. It covers the unbroken hum and the unbroken line, but not the stubborn person.
entries.definitionCN: 没有任何中断地持续。它适用于不间断的嗡鸣与不断的线，却不适用于固执的人。

entries.definition: unwilling to change one's attitude or course. It is the personal sense of persistent, usually with disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿改变态度或方向。它是 persistent 的个人义，通常带不赞成的语气。

entries.definition: remaining slowly after the cause has gone, as a smell or doubt. It stresses the slowness of departure rather than the strength of staying.
entries.definitionCN: 在成因消失后缓慢地残留，如气味或疑虑。它强调离开得慢，而不是留得有力。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: sistere 'stand', per- 'thoroughly', the participle persistens, the 16th-century entry, and the parallel noun persistence.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：sistere“站立”、per-“彻底”、分词 persistens、16 世纪的进入，以及平行的名词 persistence。

normal.en: Persistent is the standing participle: someone or something is standing thoroughly in place, and has not lifted the hand.
normal.cn: persistent 是“站立”的分词：某人或某物彻底站在原地，还没有把手拿开。

normal.en: It entered English in the 16th century for people, then moved to fevers, smells, and chemicals that also refuse to leave.
normal.cn: 它在 16 世纪先用于人，后来转到同样不肯离开的发热、气味与化学品。

normal.en: Persistent and persistence came into English on parallel tracks from the same Latin verb, not one from the other.
normal.cn: persistent 与 persistence 是从同一个拉丁动词平行进入英语的，并不是一个由另一个派生。

normal.en: Continual means repeated with gaps; continuous means without a break; persistent can mean either, depending on what it describes.
normal.cn: continual 指有间隔的重复；continuous 指没有中断；persistent 视所修饰的对象，两者都可以指。

normal.en: The same word praises a student and complains about a salesman; only the sentence decides which reading wins.
normal.cn: 同一个词既赞美学生，也抱怨推销员；只有句子能决定哪一种读法胜出。

abstract.en: A lamp that stays on after everyone has left is either a comfort or a waste, depending on who is paying.
abstract.cn: 所有人都离开后还亮着的灯，可能是安慰，也可能是浪费，取决于谁付电费。

abstract.en: A rumour is persistent because it asks nothing of the people who repeat it.
abstract.cn: 传闻之所以挥之不去，是因为它对传播它的人毫无要求。

abstract.en: A tradition survives by being boring enough to repeat and useful enough to keep.
abstract.cn: 传统之所以存续，是因为它无聊到可以重复，又有用到值得保留。

examples.en: The persistent noise from the fridge turned out to be a loose fan.
examples.cn: 冰箱那持续不断的噪音，最后查出来是风扇松了。

examples.en: Persistent organic pollutants travel thousands of kilometres.
examples.cn: 持久性有机污染物会迁移数千公里。

examples.en: She was persistent enough to get the archive opened after hours.
examples.cn: 她够执着，让档案馆在下班后重新开门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破西斯特恩特」——破了阻力还“死”站着不走，像钉子一样钉在原地 → persistent 坚持不懈的；持续不退的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 persistens，即 persistere「站稳、持续」的现在分词，由 per-「彻底」+ sistere「站立」构成（*sta-「站立」词根）；后缀 -ent 为拉丁分词词尾。核心是「按钮一直被按着，灯始终亮着」。同族含 persist、persistence、persistently；perseverant 出自另一动词 perseverare。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of persistent all describe a lamp that stays lit. What changes is what keeps it burning: a person's will, a condition's duration, a fault's return, a stain's resistance, a chemical's half-life, a disk, a symptom, a salesman, or a tradition.
sensesIntro.cn: persistent 的九个义项都描述一盏持续亮着的灯。变化的是谁让它烧着：人的意志、状况的时长、故障的回归、污渍的抵抗、化学品的半衰期、一块磁盘、一个症状、一个推销员，还是一项传统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a button held down so the lamp stays lit, and no ordinary attempt can switch it off.
core.cn: 核心意象：按钮被一直按着，灯始终亮着，普通的办法都关不掉。

branches.en: THE HOLDING PERSON: the admiring and the annoying readings of the same upright posture.
branches.cn: 按住的人：同一个挺立姿势的赞美读法与烦人读法。

branches.en: THE STUBBORN LIGHT: unbroken duration, repeated return, and resistance to removal.
branches.cn: 倔强的光：不间断的时长、反复的回归，以及对去除的抵抗。

branches.en: TECHNICAL STAYING: pollutants that will not break down, and data that survives a restart.
branches.cn: 技术性的停留：不分解的污染物，以及挺过重启的数据。

branches.en: THE BODY: a fever or infection that outlasts its expected course.
branches.cn: 身体：超过预期病程的发热或感染。

branches.en: THE LONGEST LIGHT: a custom or species carried across generations.
branches.cn: 最长的光：跨越世代被传下去的习惯或物种。

intro.en: Persistent is persist plus -ent, the Latin present-participle ending. Persist is persistere, per- 'thoroughly' + sistere 'stand'. The family includes the noun persistence, the adverb persistently, and the sistere clan: assist, insist, resist, consist.
intro.cn: persistent 是 persist 加 -ent，即拉丁现在分词词尾。persist 是 persistere，即 per-“彻底”+ sistere“站立”。词族包含名词 persistence、副词 persistently，以及 sistere 家族：assist、insist、resist、consist。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is sistere 'stand', persistere 'stand firm', and the participle persistens. The root *sta- 'stand' also gives English stand, stable, station, and statue.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 sistere“站立”、persistere“站稳”、分词 persistens。词根 *sta-“站立”还产生英语 stand（站立）、stable（稳固）、station（站点）与 statue（雕像）。

items.meaningCN: 站稳的、持续的（-ent 分词词尾）
items.example: A persistent infection needs a longer course.
items.exampleCN: 持续不退的感染需要更长的疗程。

items.example: The custom persisted into the next century.
items.exampleCN: 这个习俗延续到了下个世纪。

items.example: Persistence carried the project to the end.
items.exampleCN: 坚持把项目带到了终点。

core_image: 一群小孩在挂满纸剪花朵的院子里围坐听老师讲故事
scene: 早晨的巷口，家长牵着孩子走进一道矮栅栏门。 Every morning she walks her son to the kindergarten and waves at the gate.

senses.title: A school for children before primary school
senses.definition: an institution where children too young for school learn through play
senses.definitionCN: 供未到上学年龄的儿童以游戏方式学习的机构
senses.example: The kindergarten takes children from three years old.
senses.exampleCN: 这所幼儿园招收满三岁的孩子。
senses.why: The name literally means a garden for children, and the garden idea has stayed with the institution.
senses.whyCN: 名字字面就是「儿童的花园」，而花园这个意象一直留在这类机构身上。

senses.title: The year before primary school
senses.definition: the final pre-school year, treated as a stage rather than a place
senses.definitionCN: 上学前的最后一年，被当成一个阶段而非一处场所
senses.example: She learned to write her name in kindergarten.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学前那一年学会了写自己的名字。
senses.why: A place word easily becomes a time word, because the year and the room are experienced together.
senses.whyCN: 地点词很容易变成时间词，因为那一年和那间屋子是一起经历的。

senses.title: A play-based first school
senses.definition: the style of early teaching in which play rather than lessons comes first
senses.definitionCN: 以游戏为主、而不是以课程为先的早期教学方式
senses.example: This kindergarten builds its whole day around play.
senses.exampleCN: 这家幼儿园整天的安排都围绕游戏。
senses.why: The founding idea of such schools was to let children grow like plants, so the word also names a method.
senses.whyCN: 这类学校的创立理念是让孩子像植物一样生长，所以这个词也指一种方法。

intro.en: Kindergarten is a German coinage that English borrowed whole, a rare case of an everyday English word invented by a nineteenth-century educator.
intro.cn: kindergarten 是德语新造词，被英语整体借入，是罕见的由十九世纪教育家发明、如今天天使用的英语词。

items.en: The two parts are German Kinder, children, and Garten, garden.
items.cn: 两个部分是德语 Kinder（儿童）与 Garten（花园）。

items.en: The German educator Friedrich Froebel coined the word for his play-centred schools for small children.
items.cn: 德国教育家福禄贝尔为他那些以游戏为中心的幼儿学校造出这个词。

items.en: The word travelled with the movement to Britain and the United States in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词随着这场教育运动在十九世纪传到英国和美国。

items.en: English kept the German spelling, though the plural follows English rules.
items.cn: 英语保留了德语拼写，但复数按英语规则加 -s。

items.en: In American use the word came to mean the first year of formal school rather than a separate garden-like institution.
items.cn: 在美式用法里，这个词指正式上学的第一年，而不完全是独立的「花园式」机构。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words sharing the garden part or the child part; the near-meaning group holds other kinds of early-childhood care.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「花园」或「儿童」部分的词；近义组收其他形式的幼儿照护机构。

entries.definition: The second half of the word, a plot of ground for plants.
entries.definitionCN: 这个词的后半，指种花木的园地。

entries.definition: A class of things, spelled like the opening of this word but with no family link.
entries.definitionCN: 指类别，开头字母与本词相同，只是拼写巧合。

entries.definition: The English sense of the German first half.
entries.definitionCN: 对应德语前半部分的英语词，指儿童。

entries.definition: A place caring for very young children, often from infancy.
entries.definitionCN: 英式常用，照看更小的孩子，有的从婴儿期开始。

entries.definition: A pre-primary group or class, and the adjective for the age.
entries.definitionCN: 指学前班，也作形容词表示入小学前的。

entries.definition: An informal gathering where small children play together.
entries.definitionCN: 英式说法，指幼儿一起玩的非正式小组。

normalIntro.en: These hooks take the word apart into children and a garden, and follow it to the classroom.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词拆成「儿童」和「花园」，再把它领到教室里。

normal.en: Kinder is German for children, as in the word for children's clothes.
normal.cn: Kinder 是德语「儿童」，德语里童装也用这个词。

normal.en: Garten is German for garden.
normal.cn: Garten 是德语「花园」。

normal.en: The English plural is kindergartens, with -s.
normal.cn: 英语复数是 kindergartens，加 -s。

normal.en: Froebel founded it as a garden where children grow.
normal.cn: 福禄贝尔把它办成让孩子生长的花园。

normal.en: In the United States it is often the first year of school.
normal.cn: 在美国它常指正式上学的第一年。

abstract.en: A garden for children means nobody is expected to sit still all day.
abstract.cn: 儿童的花园意味着没人被要求整天坐直。

abstract.en: The word is a small monument to one man's idea about how children learn.
abstract.cn: 这个词是某人对「孩子怎样学」这一想法留下的一块小小纪念碑。

abstract.en: A borrowed word can carry a whole teaching method inside it.
abstract.cn: 一个借来的词可以把整套教学方法一起搬进来。

examples.en: The kindergarten closes early on Fridays.
examples.cn: 幼儿园周五提前关门。

examples.en: He cried on his first day at kindergarten.
examples.cn: 他第一天上幼儿园就哭了。

examples.en: Two kindergartens stand on the same street.
examples.cn: 同一条街上有两家幼儿园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坑的噶藤」——小孩在花园的藤架下挖坑玩，就是幼儿园

root: 德语复合词，Kinder（儿童）加 Garten（花园），由教育家福禄贝尔创办幼儿学校时创用，十九世纪进入英语，形成沿用至今的学前教育称谓。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the school itself, the pre-school year, and the play-first method behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：幼儿园这个机构、上学前的那一年，以及它背后以游戏为先的方法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small children growing in a fenced garden of paper flowers.
core.cn: 核心意象：小孩子在纸花满墙的园子里生长。

branches.en: THE GARDEN LINE: a place and a method of growth.
branches.cn: 花园这条线：一处地方，也是一种生长方法。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR LINE: the place turns into a year.
branches.cn: 日历这条线：场所变成一个年份。

branches.en: THE GATE LINE: the morning handover at the fence.
branches.cn: 门口这条线：早晨在栅栏边的交接。

branches.en: THE FIRST STEP LINE: the earliest step outside the family.
branches.cn: 第一步这条线：走出家门的第一步。

branches.en: THE PLAY LINE: learning hidden inside play.
branches.cn: 游戏这条线：学习藏在游戏里。

intro.en: Because the word was borrowed whole, English adds only an English plural and a personal noun; the inner parts belong to German.
intro.cn: 因为整词借入，英语只加了英语复数和个人名词，内部成分仍属德语。
